Others punctuate thus: *Who will grant me that they may be marked down in a book?* Then they add, [[19:24|With an iron pen and in a plate of lead|stilo ferreo et plumbi lamina]], that is, if it is little for them to be written in a book, I desire that they be written with an iron pen on a plate of lead. For such a mass of lead keeps the letters inscribed on it for a long time. Others read and punctuate thus: *Who will grant me that they may be marked down in a book with an iron pen or a plate of lead?* Which again is explained in two ways. First, *Let them be marked down in a book with an iron pen or a plate of lead*, that is, or in such material. Secondly, *or a plate of lead*, that is, let them be written in a book with an iron pen, or with a plate of lead. [[19:24|or else be graven with an instrument in flint stone?|Vel certe sculpantur in silice]] For flint, as it receives an inscription with the greatest difficulty, so it keeps it the longest. Some read: *Vel celte sculpantur* [*celte*, with a chisel: the Douay's *with an instrument*]. And Albert asserts that *celte* is an indeclinable noun, signifying a mason's tool with which the hardest stones are carved. But in the Mammotrectus of the Bible [a medieval glossary of the Bible's words] it is read that *celte* is an ablative, and is declined *celtis, celtis, celti*; and that it signifies an iron tool suited for carving. In this manner the Lord commands the prophet Habacuc: [[Hab 2:2|Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables: that he that readeth it may run over it|Scribe visum, et explana eum super tabulam, ut percurrat qui legerit eum]]. And Isaias too is bidden: [[Is 8:1|Take thee a great book, and write in it|Sume tibi librum grandem, et scribe in eo]].

paras.t: Deinde exprimit hos sermones notabilissimos, æterna memoria dignos. Scio enim quod Redemptor meus vivit. In Scripturis Scire, frequenter pro Credere sumitur, ut quum Jeremiæ decimo legitur: Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus. Hoc nempe est articulus fidei, hominem sine gratia nil posse meritorie agere. Apostolus quoque ad Timotheum: Scito quod in novissimis diebus instabunt tempora periculosa. Et Salomon in Ecclesiaste: Scito quod pro omnibus his adducet te Deus in judicium. Sic et modo Scire accipitur. Unde, ad insinuandum immobile fidei suæ robur ac certitudinem, Scio, inquit, videlicet revelatione divina et fide, quod Redemptor meus vivit, id est unigenitus Filius Dei, qui secundum divinitatem suam æternaliter et invariabiliter vivit vita actualissima, deliciosissima et perfecta: imo ipse est vivens et vita, superessentiale et superbeatissimum vivere, unaque vita cum Patre. Propter quod ait: Sicut habet Pater vitam in semetipso, sic dedit et Filio vitam habere in semetipso.
paras.en: Then he utters these most notable words, worthy of eternal memory: [[19:25|For I know that my Redeemer liveth|Scio enim quod Redemptor meus vivit]]. In the Scriptures *to know* is often taken for *to believe*, as when it is read in the tenth chapter of Jeremias: [[Jer 10:23|I know, O Lord, that the way of a man is not his|Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus]]. For it is an article of faith that man without grace can do nothing meritoriously. The Apostle too to Timothy: [[2 Tim 3:1|Know also this, that in the last days shall come dangerous times|Scito quod in novissimis diebus instabunt tempora periculosa]] And Solomon in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 11:9|know that for all these God will bring thee into judgment|Scito quod pro omnibus his adducet te Deus in judicium]]. And so *to know* is taken here. Hence, to suggest the unshaken strength and certainty of his faith, he says: *I know*, namely by divine revelation and by faith, *that my Redeemer liveth*, that is, the only-begotten Son of God, who according to his divinity lives eternally and unchangeably a life most actual, most delightful and perfect: nay, he is himself the living one and life, a superessential and most supremely blessed living, one life with the Father. For which reason he says: [[John 5:26|For as the Father hath life in himself|Sicut habet Pater vitam in semetipso]]

paras.t: Præterea, juxta Thomam, noverat Job, Deo revelante, quod propter protoplasti parentis peccatum, damnationi obnoxium esset genus humanum, a qua per unigeniti Filii Dei incarnationem ac passionem disposito tempore redimeretur. Sed quoniam Redemptorem noverat verum Deum sempiterne viventem, non ait, Credo quod Redemptor meus vivet; sed, Vivit: sicut et Christus ait Judæis, Antequam Abraham fieret, ego sum. De quo ad Hebræos ait Apostolus: Jesus Christus heri, et hodie; ipse et in sæcula. Christus quippe, secundum doctores, supponit hypostasim increatam æternam. Propter quod Judas ait in sua Canonica: Jesus populum salvans ex Ægypto.
paras.en: Moreover, according to Thomas, Job knew by God's revelation that because of the sin of our first parent the human race was liable to damnation, from which it would be redeemed at the appointed time by the incarnation and passion of the only-begotten Son of God. But because he knew the Redeemer to be true God, living eternally, he does not say, I believe that my Redeemer *will live*, but *liveth*: as Christ too says to the Jews: [[John 8:58|before Abraham was made, I AM|Antequam Abraham fieret, ego sum]]. Of whom the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 13:8|Jesus Christ, yesterday, and today: and the same for ever|Jesus Christus heri, et hodie; ipse et in sæcula]] For *Christ*, according to the doctors, stands for the uncreated, eternal hypostasis [that is, the name *Christ* refers to the eternal Person of the Word, so that what is said of the man is said of God]. For which reason Jude says in his canonical epistle: [[Jude 1:5|Jesus, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt|Jesus populum salvans ex Ægypto]].

paras.t: Et in novissimo die status hujus sæculi, videlicet in fine mundi, quando generatio cessabit, de terra surrecturus sum, id est, corpus meum ex cineribus suis reparabitur, et anima mea illi reunietur: sicque qui per mortem cecidi, per resuscitationem de terra tunc surgam. Resurrectio enim est ejus quod cecidit, secundum Damascenum. Ex hoc elucescit, quod juxta sententiam sancti Job, mundus finietur, quantum ad generationem et corruptionem, ac temporis cursum; et quod generalis resurrectio fiet in termino mundi, non ante, nec postea, neque multoties. Ex quibus confunditur error quorumdam Platonicorum et hæreticorum, dicentium, post certa temporum intervalla, redeuntibus ad eosdem situs sideribus, corrupta reparari, mortuosque ad hanc vitam reverti. Ad quod etiam quidam allegabant illud Ecclesiastæ: Quid est quod fuit? ipsum quod futurum est. Quid est quod factum est? ipsum quod faciendum est. Nihil sub sole novum, nec valet quisquam dicere, Ecce hoc recens est: jam enim præcessit in sæculis quæ fuerunt ante nos. Sed (ut B. Augustinus in libro de Civitate Dei exponit) hoc Salomon loquitur non de eisdem numero, sed specie. Denique, verbo inducto Christus conformiter loquens: Ego, inquit, resuscitabo eum in novissimo die. Et Martha ait de fratre suo: Scio quia resurget in resurrectione in novissimo die.
paras.en: [[19:25|and in the last day|Et in novissimo die]] of the state of this world, namely at the end of the world, when generation will cease, [[19:25|I shall rise out of the earth|de terra surrecturus sum]], that is, my body will be restored from its ashes, and my soul reunited to it: and so I who fell by death shall then rise from the earth by resurrection. For resurrection is of that which fell, according to Damascene. From this it is clear that, according to the judgment of holy Job, the world will come to an end as to generation and corruption and the course of time; and that the general resurrection will take place at the end of the world, not before, nor after, nor many times. By which is confounded the error of certain Platonists and heretics, who say that after certain intervals of time, when the stars return to the same positions, things corrupted are restored and the dead return to this life. For this some also alleged that saying of Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 1:9|What is it that hath been? the same thing that shall be. What is it that hath been done? the same that shall be done|Quid est quod factum est? ipsum quod faciendum est]] [[Eccles 1:10|Nothing under the sun is new, neither is any man able to say: Behold this is new: for it hath already gone before in the ages that were before us|Nihil sub sole novum, nec valet quisquam dicere, Ecce hoc recens est: jam enim præcessit in sæculis quæ fuerunt ante nos]] But (as blessed Augustine expounds in the book of the City of God) Solomon says this not of the same things in number, but in kind. Further, Christ, speaking in agreement with the word brought in here, says: [[John 6:40|I will raise him up in the last day|Ego, inquit, resuscitabo eum in novissimo die]]. And Martha says of her brother: [[John 11:24|I know that he shall rise again, in the resurrection at the last day|Scio quia resurget in resurrectione in novissimo die]].

paras.t: Et rursum circumdabor pelle mea, istam cum carnibus et ossibus recipiendo. Quo verbo damnantur hæretici, asserentes quod corpora suscitanda, erunt aurea sive cœlestia. Et in carne mea, eadem videlicet qua nunc tegitur anima mea, videbo Deum salvatorem meum, divinitatem ejus videndo clare per speciem oculo interiori, humanitatem vero ipsius oculo corporali; nec dubium quin et oculi interiores illam intellectualiter sint visuri, sicut et angeli eam adspiciunt. Corpora autem suscitata, quatuor dotibus erunt ornata et glorificata, videlicet impassibilitate, agilitate, claritate et subtilitate: idcirco contemplationem, libertatem, et beatitudinem animæ nequaquam impedient, sed augebunt, præsertim quum anima naturaliter forma sit corporis: ideoque naturaliter inclinatur ad informationem ipsius. Quem visurus sum ego ipse, videlicet in eadem carne et in eadem anima, ex quibus modo subsisto, et oculi mei conspecturi sunt: per modum jam tactum; et non alius loco mei, quamvis alii multi mecum simul sint illum visuri. Unusquisque enim propriam mercedem recipiet. Sacrilegus impiusque Porphyrius arguit Christianos maximæ stultitiæ, eo quod dicant mundum finiendum, et corpora suscitanda, eo quod corpus contemplationem impediat; sed ex beatissimo Job ejus insania apertissime reprobatur.
paras.en: [[19:26|And I shall be clothed again with my skin|Et rursum circumdabor pelle mea]], receiving it back with flesh and bones. By this word the heretics are condemned who assert that the bodies to be raised will be of gold or of heavenly stuff. [[19:26|and in my flesh|Et in carne mea]], namely the same with which my soul is now covered, [[19:26|I shall see my God|videbo Deum]] my Saviour [Denis reads *Deum salvatorem meum*, God my Saviour], seeing his divinity clearly by sight with the inward eye, and his humanity with the bodily eye; nor is there any doubt that the inward eyes too will see that humanity intellectually, as the angels also behold it. The risen bodies will be adorned and glorified with four endowments, namely impassibility, agility, brightness and subtlety: therefore they will in no way hinder the contemplation, freedom and beatitude of the soul, but will increase them, especially since the soul is by nature the form of the body, and so is naturally inclined to informing it. [[19:27|Whom I myself shall see|Quem visurus sum ego ipse]], namely in the same flesh and the same soul of which I now consist, [[19:27|and my eyes shall behold|et oculi mei conspecturi sunt]], in the manner already touched on; [[19:27|and not another|et non alius]] in my place, although many others will see him together with me. [[1 Cor 3:8|every man shall receive his own reward|Unusquisque enim propriam mercedem recipiet]]. The sacrilegious and impious Porphyry accuses Christians of the greatest folly for saying that the world will end and bodies be raised, on the ground that the body hinders contemplation; but his madness is most openly refuted from most blessed Job.

paras.t: Reposita est hæc spes mea de futura glorificatione corporis mei et animæ meæ, in sinu meo, id est in secreto et intimo cordis mei, tanquam pretiosissimus atque carissimus mentis meæ thesaurus. Sic sumitur sinus apud Joannem, ubi legitur: Unigenitus Filius qui est in sinu Patris, ipse enarravit. Præterea, de hac resurrectione Daniel scribit: Multi de his qui dormiunt in pulvere terræ, evigilabunt, alii in vitam æternam, alii in opprobrium. Et Isaias: Mortui tui vivent, interfectique mei resurgent.
paras.en: [[19:27|this my hope is laid up|Reposita est hæc spes mea]] of the future glorification of my body and soul [[19:27|in my bosom|in sinu meo]], that is, in the secret and inmost part of my heart, as the most precious and dearest treasure of my mind. So *bosom* is taken in John, where it is read: [[John 1:18|the only begotten Son who is in the Bosom of the Father, he hath declared him|Unigenitus Filius qui est in sinu Patris, ipse enarravit]]. Moreover, of this resurrection Daniel writes: [[Dan 12:2|many of those that sleep in the dust of the earth, shall awake: some unto life everlasting, and others unto reproach|Multi de his qui dormiunt in pulvere terræ, evigilabunt, alii in vitam æternam, alii in opprobrium]]. And Isaias: [[Is 26:19|Thy dead men shall live, my slain shall rise again|Mortui tui vivent, interfectique mei resurgent]].

paras.t: Quare ergo nunc dicitis vos contra me disputantes: Persequamur eum, id est, affligamus hunc Job, eum reprobando tanquam erroneum; et radicem verbi, id est verbum fundamentale ac firmum, inveniamus contra eum, dicta ejus totaliter destruendo?
paras.en: [[19:28|Why then do you say now|Quare ergo nunc dicitis]], you who dispute against me: [[19:28|Let us persecute him|Persequamur eum]], that is, let us afflict this Job, refuting him as one in error; [[19:28|and let us find occasion of word against him?|et radicem verbi inveniamus contra eum?]] [literally *let us find the root of the word against him*], that is, a fundamental and firm word, destroying his sayings altogether?

paras.t: Fugite ergo a facie gladii, id est, divinæ justitiæ sententiam contra vos timete, et pœnitendo salubriter declinate. De quo gladio in Apocalypsi habetur: De ore ejus gladius ex utraque parte acutus exibat. Et in Deuteronomio Dominus protestatur: Si acuero ut fulgur gladium meum, et arripuerit judicium manus mea, reddam ultionem hostibus meis. Ideo subditur: quoniam ultor iniquitatum gladius est, id est, divinæ justitiæ sententia peccata faciet vindicari, seu juste puniri. De quo gladio dicitur Christo in Psalmo: Accingere gladio tuo super femur tuum, potentissime. De hac ultione Dominus ait per Malachiam: Ecce dies veniet succensa quasi caminus; et erunt omnes superbi et omnes facientes impietatem, stipula; et inflammabit eos dies veniens, quæ non derelinquet eis radicem. Unde dicit et Judas: Ecce venit Dominus in sanctis millibus suis facere judicium, et arguere omnes impios de omnibus operibus impietatis eorum. Et scitote esse judicium Dei, tam particulare, quo judicat unumquemque dum moritur, quam universale, quo in die novissimo judicaturus est omnes, juxta illud Ecclesiastæ: Cuncta quæ fiunt, adducet Deus in judicium pro omni errato, sive bonum sit, sive malum. Apostolus quoque: Omnes, inquit, nos manifestari oportet ante tribunal Christi.
paras.en: [[19:29|Flee then from the face of the sword|Fugite ergo a facie gladii]], that is, fear the sentence of divine justice against you, and turn it aside by wholesome penance. Of this sword we have in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 1:16|from his mouth came out a sharp two-edged sword|De ore ejus gladius ex utraque parte acutus exibat]]. And in Deuteronomy the Lord declares: [[Deut 32:41|If I shall whet my sword as the lightning, and my hand take hold on judgment: I will render vengeance to my enemies|Si acuero ut fulgur gladium meum, et arripuerit judicium manus mea, reddam ultionem hostibus meis]]. Therefore it is added: [[19:29|for the sword is the revenger of iniquities|quoniam ultor iniquitatum gladius est]], that is, the sentence of divine justice will cause sins to be avenged, or justly punished. Of this sword it is said to Christ in the Psalm: [[Ps 44:4|Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O thou most mighty.|Accingere gladio tuo super femur tuum, potentissime.]] Of this vengeance the Lord speaks through Malachias: [[Mal 4:1|the day shall come kindled as a furnace: and all the proud, and all that do wickedly shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall set them on fire, saith the Lord of hosts, it shall not leave them root|dies veniet succensa quasi caminus; et erunt omnes superbi et omnes facientes impietatem, stipula; et inflammabit eos dies veniens, quæ non derelinquet eis radicem]]. Hence Jude too says: [[Jude 1:14|Behold, the Lord cometh with thousands of his saints|Ecce venit Dominus in sanctis millibus suis]] [[Jude 1:15|To execute judgment upon all and to reprove all the ungodly for all the works of their ungodliness|facere judicium, et arguere omnes impios de omnibus operibus impietatis eorum]]. [[19:29|and know ye that there is a judgment|Et scitote esse judicium]] of God, both particular, by which he judges each one when he dies, and universal, by which at the last day he will judge all, according to that of Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 12:14|all things that are done, God will bring into judgment for every error, whether it be good or evil|Cuncta quæ fiunt, adducet Deus in judicium pro omni errato, sive bonum sit, sive malum]] The Apostle too: [[2 Cor 5:10|we must all be manifested before the judgment seat of Christ|Omnes, inquit, nos manifestari oportet ante tribunal Christi]].

paras.t: Ex istis, beatus Job amicis suis ostendit, quod non desperavit, nec circa providentiam Dei erravit ut ipsi: ideo consulit eis pœnitentiam salutarem.
paras.en: By these things blessed Job shows his friends that he has not despaired, nor erred about the providence of God as they have: and therefore he counsels them to wholesome penance.

19.title: De mysteriis ejusdem capituli nonidecimi
19.title_en: On the mysteries of the same nineteenth chapter

paras.t: Sanctum Job fuisse evidentissimam Christi figuram, frequenter inductum est. Hinc præsens capitulum pro maxima sui parte de Christo potest exponi: quod breviter tangendum opinor.
paras.en: That holy Job was a most evident figure of Christ has often been shown. Hence the present chapter can for the most part be expounded of Christ: which I think should be touched on briefly.

paras.t: Respondens Job dixit: Usquequo affligitis animam meam, et atteritis me sermonibus? Anima justi ipsa falsitate affligitur, præsertim dum impios audit æquitati resistere, et contradicere veritati. Job ergo, qui interpretatur dolens, id est Christus propter nos passus, qui ait in Psalmo, Ego sum pauper et dolens: de quo loquitur Isaias, Dolores nostros ipse portavit; dixit Scribis et Pharisæis æquivalenter verba prætacta, quum ait ad eos: Quid me tentatis, hypocritæ? Marcus quoque ait, quod Jesus circumspiciens Pharisæos cum ira, contristatus est super cæcitate cordis eorum, qui inierunt contra eum consilium, eo quod sabbato curasset infirmum. Multa insuper blasphemiis plena contra Christum locuti sunt, dicendo: Dæmonium habet. Insanit; quid eum auditis? Seducit turbas. Homo vorax, potator vini, amicus peccatorum et publicanorum. In principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia. Hic blasphemat. Reus est mortis. Hinc afflictus est Christus non ex impatientia, sed zelo justitiæ: imo ex caritate errantibus condolens naturali seu etiam caritativo affectu, et propter inhonorationem Patris æterni.
paras.en: [[19:1|Job answered, and said|Respondens Job dixit]]: [[19:2|How long do you afflict my soul, and break me in pieces with words?|Usquequo affligitis animam meam, et atteritis me sermonibus?]] The soul of the just is afflicted by falsehood itself, especially when it hears the wicked resist equity and contradict the truth. Job, then, whose name is interpreted *grieving*, that is, Christ who suffered for us, who says in the Psalm, [[Ps 68:30|I am poor and sorrowful|Ego sum pauper et dolens]], and of whom Isaias says, He [[Is 53:4|carried our sorrows|Dolores nostros ipse portavit]], said to the Scribes and Pharisees words equivalent to those just quoted, when he said to them: [[Matt 22:18|Why do you tempt me, ye hypocrites?|Quid me tentatis, hypocritæ?]] Mark too says that Jesus, [[Mark 3:5|looking round about|circumspiciens]] on the Pharisees [[Mark 3:5|with anger|cum ira]], was [[Mark 3:5|grieved for the blindness of their hearts|contristatus est super cæcitate cordis eorum]], who had taken counsel against him[[Mark 3:6||]] because he had healed a sick man on the sabbath. Moreover they spoke many things full of blasphemy against Christ, saying: [[John 10:20|He hath a devil and is mad. Why hear you him?|Dæmonium habet. Insanit; quid eum auditis?]] [[John 7:12|he seduceth the people|Seducit turbas]]. [[Matt 11:19|a man that is a glutton and a wine drinker, a friend of publicans and sinners|Homo vorax, potator vini, amicus peccatorum et publicanorum]]. [[Matt 9:34|By the prince of devils he casteth out devils|In principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia]]. [[Matt 9:3|He blasphemeth|Hic blasphemat]]. [[Matt 26:66|He is guilty of death|Reus est mortis]]. Hence Christ was afflicted, not out of impatience but out of zeal for justice; nay rather out of charity, grieving with those who erred with a natural and also a charitable affection, and on account of the dishonour done to the eternal Father.

paras.t: Quoniam ergo tam sæpe confusive allocuti sunt Christum, seu locuti sunt de eo, rite adjungit: En decies confunditis me, quantum in vobis est. Sicque ponitur numerus determinatus pro indeterminato, sicut in Apocalypsi, quum dicitur: Regnaverunt cum Christo mille annis. Et non erubescitis opprimentes me innocentem, justum et pauperem: quod vitiosissimum turpissimumque consistit. In passione autem Christum corporaliter oppresserunt, quamvis virtutes et patientiam animæ ejus opprimere non valerent. Hinc Sapiens dixisse eos scribit: Opprimamus justum, quoniam contrarius est operibus nostris, et filium Dei se nominat. Denique, quidam malignantis sunt animi et mentis crudelis: qui si viderint quempiam a multis vexari, sæpiusque confundi, non condolent nec succurrunt; sed potius injuriantibus se jungendo, afflictionem augent afflicti: in quibus nulla est verecundia, nulla pietas aut honestas; sed inhumani atque brutales sunt tales, instar canum mordentes corrosum. Nos ergo, etiamsi a quo graviter læsi fuerimus, tunc ei potissime ignoscamus, compatiamur, suffragemur, dum eum aliunde videmus aut scimus affligi.
paras.en: Since, then, they so often addressed Christ, or spoke of him, so as to confound him, he fittingly adds: [[19:3|Behold, these ten times you confound me|En decies confunditis me]], as far as lies in you. And so a definite number is put for an indefinite, as in the Apocalypse, where it is said: They [[Apoc 20:4|reigned with Christ a thousand years|Regnaverunt cum Christo mille annis]]. And [[19:3|are not ashamed to oppress me|non erubescitis opprimentes me]], an innocent man, just and poor: which is a most vicious and most shameful thing. In the passion they oppressed Christ in body, though they could not oppress the virtues and the patience of his soul. Hence the Wise Man writes that they said: Let us oppress the just man, because [[Wis 2:12|he is contrary to our doings|contrarius est operibus nostris]], and [[Wis 2:13|calleth himself the son of God|filium Dei se nominat]] [the margin gives Wis. ii, 12, 13; the opening words, *Let us oppress the just man*, echo 2:10, *Let us oppress the poor just man*, where 2:12 has *Let us lie in wait for the just*]. Lastly, there are some of malignant spirit and cruel mind who, if they see anyone harassed by many and often confounded, do not grieve with him or help him, but rather, joining themselves to those who wrong him, increase the affliction of the afflicted: in whom there is no shame, no piety or decency; but such men are inhuman and brutish, like dogs biting one already gnawed. Let us, then, even if someone has wronged us gravely, forgive him then above all, have compassion on him and stand by him, when we see or know that he is afflicted from another quarter.

paras.t: Nempe, si ignoravi, mecum erit ignorantia mea. Ignorantiam esse in Christo multiplicem arbitrabantur Judæi; et quæ inter se occulte contra eum tractabant, ipsum putabant nescire. Et experientes demum sapientiam ejus, mirantes sciscitabantur: Unde hic scit litteras, quum non didicerit? Imo, quasi errantem et turbas fallentem, dicebant se persequi eum. Quibus verbum præscriptum Christus potuit fari, velut si diceret: Tot, tanta, et talia ac taliter coram vobis miracula facio, quod de veritate doctrinæ meæ rationabiliter dubitare nequaquam valetis, quoniam Deus testimonium falsitati non præbet: quod si ignoro scienda, ignorantia mea redundabit in me.
paras.en: [[19:4|For if I have been ignorant, my ignorance shall be with me|Nempe, si ignoravi, mecum erit ignorantia mea]]. The Jews thought there was much ignorance in Christ; and what they plotted against him secretly among themselves, they thought he did not know. And when at length they found out his wisdom, they asked in wonder: [[John 7:15|How doth this man know letters, having never learned?|Unde hic scit litteras, quum non didicerit?]] [Denis has *Unde*, whence, for the Vulgate's *Quomodo*, how] Nay, they said that they were persecuting him as one who erred and led the crowds astray[[John 7:12||]][[Luke 23:2||]] [the margin gives Ibid. 12 and Luc. xxiii, apparently xxiii, 2]. To them Christ could have spoken the words set down above, as if to say: So many, so great and such miracles I work before you, and in such a way, that you can by no means reasonably doubt the truth of my doctrine, since God does not bear witness to falsehood: if then I am ignorant of what should be known, my ignorance will redound on me.

paras.t: At vos contra me erigimini. Sic sacerdotes, Scribæ et Pharisæi contra Christum se erexerunt, dicentes illud: Nos scimus quoniam hic homo peccator est; et: Nescimus unde sit. Insuper verbis et factis superbissime opposuerunt se Christo, juxta illud Psalmi: Persecuti sunt hominem inopem et mendicum, et compunctum corde mortificare. Quem psalmum de Christo litteraliter scriptum, princeps Apostolorum insinuat in Actis. Præterea, plures sunt, qui pro eo quod erigere se contra se tanquam contra passionatos, vitiosos, ac imprudentes deberent, negligunt se, et contra alios, etiam adversum meliores se erigunt, eis culpam et insipientiam imponendo, non pensantes quod in Proverbiis habetur: Justus prior accusator est sui. Quorum molestiam ferens justus, dicere potest illud Threnorum: Vide, Domine, afflictionem meam, quoniam erectus est inimicus.
paras.en: [[19:5|But you set yourselves up against me|At vos contra me erigimini]]. So the priests, Scribes and Pharisees set themselves up against Christ, saying: [[John 9:24|We know that this man is a sinner|Nos scimus quoniam hic homo peccator est]]; and: [[John 9:29|we know not from whence he is|Nescimus unde sit]]. Moreover they opposed themselves to Christ most proudly in words and deeds, according to that of the Psalm: They [[Ps 108:17|persecuted the poor man and the beggar; and the broken in heart, to put him to death|Persecuti sunt hominem inopem et mendicum, et compunctum corde mortificare]] [the margin gives the Psalm's own reading, *Persecutus est*, he persecuted]. That this psalm was written literally of Christ, the prince of the Apostles indicates in the Acts[[Acts 1:20||]]. Further, there are many who, whereas they ought to set themselves up against themselves, as against men swayed by passion, vicious and imprudent, neglect themselves, and set themselves up against others, even against their betters, laying fault and folly on them, not weighing what is had in the Proverbs: [[Prov 18:17|The just is first accuser of himself|Justus prior accusator est sui]]. The just man, bearing the annoyance they cause, can say that word of Lamentations: [[Lam 1:9|behold, O Lord, my affliction, because the enemy is lifted up|Vide, Domine, afflictionem meam, quoniam erectus est inimicus]].

paras.t: Et arguitis me opprobriis meis, id est mihi a vobis false objectis. Jam enim inductum est, quam opprobriosa verba locuti sint Christo. Ideo ait ad Patrem in Psalmo: Quoniam propter te sustinui opprobrium. Itemque: Ego factus opprobrium illis; viderunt me, et moverunt capita sua. Hinc Petrus ait Judæis: Hic est lapis qui reprobatus est a vobis ædificantibus.
paras.en: And [[19:5|reprove me with my reproaches|arguitis me opprobriis meis]], that is, those falsely laid against me by you. For it has already been shown what reproachful words they spoke to Christ. Therefore he says to the Father in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:8|Because for thy sake I have borne reproach|Quoniam propter te sustinui opprobrium]]. And again: [[Ps 108:25|I am become a reproach to them: they saw me and they shaked their heads|Ego factus opprobrium illis; viderunt me, et moverunt capita sua]]. Hence Peter says to the Jews: [[Acts 4:11|This is the stone which was rejected by you the builders|Hic est lapis qui reprobatus est a vobis ædificantibus]].

paras.t: Saltem nunc intelligite, quia Deus non æquo judicio afflixerit me, et flagellis suis me cinxerit. Judæi increduli Christum ob sua peccata juste damnatum dixerunt. Quibus Christus in cruce pendens, quum tot mirabilia fierent, dicere potuit verbum hoc, quasi diceret: Ex his mirabilibus perpendite, quod Deus Pater, seu Trinitas, non æquo judicio me affligi permisit: æquitate qua redditur cuiquam quod meruit. Hoc est, pensate quod non pro peccatis meis hæc patior, sed pro mundi offensis: quemadmodum in Isaia Pater testatur, Propter peccata populi mei percussi eum. Hoc Christus post Spiritus Sancti missionem, per os Apostolorum publice prædicavit, et per miracula declaravit. Unde in Actis Petrus loquens Judæis, Deus, inquit, patrum nostrorum glorificavit Filium suum Jesum, quem tradidistis et negastis ante faciem Pilati.
paras.en: [[19:6|At least now understand, that God hath not afflicted me with an equal judgment, and compassed me with his scourges|Saltem nunc intelligite, quia Deus non æquo judicio afflixerit me, et flagellis suis me cinxerit]]. The unbelieving Jews said that Christ was justly condemned for his sins. To them Christ, hanging on the cross while so many wonders were taking place, could have said this word, as if to say: Weigh from these wonders that God the Father, or the Trinity, has not allowed me to be afflicted with an equal judgment, that is, with the equity by which each is rendered what he has deserved. That is, consider that I suffer these things not for my own sins but for the offences of the world: as the Father testifies in Isaias, [[Is 53:8|for the wickedness of my people have I struck him|Propter peccata populi mei percussi eum]]. This Christ, after the sending of the Holy Ghost, preached publicly through the mouth of the Apostles, and made it plain by miracles. Hence in the Acts Peter, speaking to the Jews, says: [[Acts 3:13|the God of our fathers, hath glorified his Son Jesus, whom you indeed delivered up and denied before the face of Pilate|patrum nostrorum glorificavit Filium suum Jesum, quem tradidistis et negastis ante faciem Pilati]].

paras.t: Ecce clamabo vim patiens, et nemo audiet. Hoc est quod Christus ait in Psalmo: Deus meus, clamabo per diem, et non exaudies; et nocte, et non ad insipientiam mihi. Nec obstat quod ait Apostolus, quia exauditus est Christus pro sua reverentia. Ipse quoque Salvator: Pater, ego sciebam, quoniam semper me audis. Verum est enim, quod quidquid Christus ex deliberata ratione et voluntate petivit, sortitus est. Aliqua autem oravit secundum naturalem et sensitivum suæ humanitatis appetitum, in quibus fertur non exauditus: sicut quum dixit, Aufer a me calicem istum. Sed tales orationes non fuerunt proprie orationes absolute dictæ, et simpliciter fusæ. Itaque, quod ait, Nemo audiet, secundum hæc exponitur, Nullus exaudiet. Potest autem et ita exponi, Clamabo vim patiens: quia in cruce violentissimam sustinens mortem, clamavit: Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me? Et nemo audiet, id est, nullus homo succurret. Hinc ait in Psalmo: Sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit; et qui consolaretur, et non inveni.
paras.en: [[19:7|Behold I shall cry suffering violence, and no one will hear|Ecce clamabo vim patiens, et nemo audiet]]. This is what Christ says in the Psalm: [[Ps 21:3|O my God, I shall cry by day, and thou wilt not hear: and by night, and it shall not be reputed as folly in me|Deus meus, clamabo per diem, et non exaudies; et nocte, et non ad insipientiam mihi]]. Nor does it stand in the way that the Apostle says that Christ [[Heb 5:7|was heard for his reverence|exauditus est Christus pro sua reverentia]]; and the Saviour himself: Father, [[John 11:42|I knew that thou hearest me always|ego sciebam, quoniam semper me audis]]. For it is true that whatever Christ asked for with deliberate reason and will, he obtained. But some things he prayed for according to the natural and sensitive appetite of his humanity [that is, the appetite of the senses, as distinct from the deliberate will], and in these he is said not to have been heard: as when he said, [[Luke 22:42|remove this chalice from me|Aufer a me calicem istum]] [Denis has *Aufer*, take away, for the Vulgate's *transfer*]. But such prayers were not prayers properly so called, said absolutely and poured forth simply. And so what he says, [[19:7|no one will hear|Nemo audiet]], is expounded in this way: None will hear favourably [*exaudiet*: to hear and grant]. But it can also be expounded thus: [[19:7|I shall cry suffering violence|Clamabo vim patiens]], because, suffering a most violent death on the cross, he cried out: [[Matt 27:46|My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me?|Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?]] [[19:7|and no one will hear|Et nemo audiet]], that is, no man will come to help. Hence he says in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:21|I looked for one that would grieve together with me, but there was none: and for one that would comfort me, and I found none|Sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit; et qui consolaretur, et non inveni]].

paras.t: Vociferabor: quia cum clamore valido et lacrimis obtulit Christus preces Patri in nocte qua tradebatur, secundum Apostolum: et non est qui judicet; quia tunc non fuit qui judicaret Christum secundum innocentiam suam, secundum quam ab omni pœna fuisset mox præservandus; sed judicatus fuit a præside Pilato injuste. Præterea Deus frequenter electorum petitiones differt audire, et voces eorum se advertere quasi dissimulat, ut interim expurgentur, et diu clamando, copiosius præfixo tempore exaudiantur: qui hanc divinæ pietatis dispensationem non intuentes, conqueruntur se quasi relictos, seu non attentos a Deo; sed in tali dilatione habenda est patientia, certa fiducia, indefessa instantia.
paras.en: [[19:7|I shall cry aloud|Vociferabor]]: for Christ offered prayers to the Father [[Heb 5:7|with a strong cry and tears|cum clamore valido et lacrimis]] on the night in which he was betrayed, according to the Apostle; [[19:7|and there is none to judge|et non est qui judicet]]: for then there was none to judge Christ according to his innocence, by which he should at once have been kept from all punishment; but he was judged unjustly by the governor Pilate. Further, God often puts off hearing the petitions of the elect, and as it were pretends not to heed their voices, so that meanwhile they may be cleansed, and, by crying long, may be heard more abundantly at the appointed time: and those who do not see this dispensation of the divine goodness complain that they are as it were forsaken, or not heeded by God; but in such delay one must have patience, sure confidence, unwearied perseverance.

paras.t: Semitam meam circumsepsit. Processus enim conversationis Christi in sæculo isto, adversitatibus fuit repletus. Propterea ait in Psalmo: Pauper sum ego, et in laboribus a juventute mea. Et transire non possum. Christus etiam a Judæis comprehensus, ligatus et crucifixus, quamvis secundum exteriorem apparentiam, seu naturalem humanam potentiam transire hinc inde nequiverit, propter quod verba ista hoc modo ei conveniunt; nihilo minus, absolute loquendo, se ipsum eripere, excutere, transireque potuit per suam divinam potentiam, imo et per creatam suam supernaturalem potentiam. Attamen, quasi secure inter Judæos transire non valens, persecutionem illorum ad horam declinans, subtraxit se, juxta illud Joannis: Ab illo die cogitaverunt ut interficerent eum. Jesus ergo jam non in palam ambulabat apud Judæos, sed abiit in regionem juxta desertum, in civitatem quæ dicitur Ephrem, et ibi morabatur cum discipulis suis. Et in calle meo tenebras persecutionum posuit.
paras.en: [[19:8|He hath hedged in my path round about|Semitam meam circumsepsit]]. For the course of Christ's life in this world was full of adversities. Therefore he says in the Psalm: [[Ps 87:16|I am poor, and in labours from my youth|Pauper sum ego, et in laboribus a juventute mea]]. And [[19:8|I cannot pass|transire non possum]]. Christ too, seized, bound[[John 18:12||]] and crucified[[Mark 15:25||]] by the Jews [the margin gives Joann. xvi, 12, which does not fit; John 18:12 tells of the seizing and binding], though by outward appearance, or by natural human power, he could not pass hence and thence, for which reason these words fit him in this way; nevertheless, speaking absolutely, he could rescue himself, shake them off and pass through by his divine power, nay even by his created supernatural power. Yet, as one not able to pass safely among the Jews, turning aside from their persecution for a time, he withdrew himself, according to that of John: [[John 11:53|From that day therefore they devised to put him to death|Ab illo die cogitaverunt ut interficerent eum]]. [[John 11:54|Wherefore Jesus walked no more openly among the Jews: but he went into a country near the desert, unto a city that is called Ephrem. And there he abode with his disciples|Jesus ergo jam non in palam ambulabat apud Judæos, sed abiit in regionem juxta desertum, in civitatem quæ dicitur Ephrem, et ibi morabatur cum discipulis suis]]. And [[19:8|in my way|in calle meo]] he hath set [[19:8|darkness|tenebras]] of persecutions.

paras.t: Spoliavit me gloria mea. Christus enim ad tempus inclytæ exstitit famæ apud vulgares, præcipue quando (ut Evangelistæ testantur) omnis populus gaudebat in omnibus quæ magnifice fiebant per illum, atque dicebat: Quia nunquam sic apparuit in Israel; et: Propheta magnus surrexit in nobis. In die quoque Palmarum honor et gloria ei a populo eminentissime impendebantur. Sed in die Parasceves Pater spoliavit permissive Christum hac gloria, in tantum, ut universus populus eum negaret, ac diceret: Sanguis ejus super nos, et super filios nostros. Petivitque latronem potius quam Christum dimitti. Et abstulit coronam de capite meo: quia videlicet Pater misit Filium in maxima paupertate, ita quod temporaliter non regnavit, nec in primo adventu judicium retributionis exercuit: sicque abstulit ei Pater coronam ad tempus, qua dignus jugiter fuit. Nam et quum Judæi venturi erant ut raperent eum, et regem facerent, Patre volente mox fugit in montem.
paras.en: [[19:9|He hath stripped me of my glory|Spoliavit me gloria mea]]. For Christ was for a time of renowned fame among the common people, especially when (as the Evangelists testify) [[Luke 13:17|all the people rejoiced for all the things that were gloriously done by him|omnis populus gaudebat in omnibus quæ magnifice fiebant per illum]] [Denis has *in omnibus quæ magnifice fiebant per illum* for the Vulgate's *in universis, quæ gloriose fiebant ab eo*], and said: [[Matt 9:33|Never was the like seen in Israel|nunquam sic apparuit in Israel]]; and: [[Luke 7:16|A great prophet is risen up among us|Propheta magnus surrexit in nobis]]. On Palm Sunday, too, honour and glory were paid him by the people most eminently[[Matt 21:8||]][[Matt 21:9||]]. But on the day of the Parasceve [the Preparation, that is, Good Friday] the Father, by permitting it, stripped Christ of this glory, so far that the whole people denied him and said: [[Matt 27:25|His blood be upon us and upon our children|Sanguis ejus super nos, et super filios nostros]]. And they asked that the robber rather than Christ be released[[Luke 23:18||]]. And [[19:9|hath taken the crown from my head|abstulit coronam de capite meo]]: that is, because the Father sent the Son in the greatest poverty, so that he did not reign in temporal things, nor exercise the judgment of retribution in his first coming: and so the Father took from him for a time the crown of which he was ever worthy. For when the Jews would come [[John 6:15|to take him by force and make him king|ut raperent eum, et regem facerent]], at the Father's will he at once [[John 6:15|fled again into the mountains|fugit in montem]].

paras.t: Destruxit me undique, id est, toto corpore vulneribus lacerari permisit; et pereo, id est, corporaliter morior: secundum illud Isaiæ, Justus perit, et non est qui recogitet. Et quasi avulsæ arbori abstulit spem meam. Pro Judæorum conversione Christus multipliciter laboravit, et spem quamdam seu exspectationem de eorum conversione tunc habuit: quæ, quantum ad majorem populi illius partem, ablata est ei, quando populus ille in perfidia sua obstinatus effectus est. Hinc in Isaia loquitur Christus: Ego dixi: In vacuum laboravi, sine causa et vane consumpsi fortitudinem meam.
paras.en: [[19:10|He hath destroyed me on every side|Destruxit me undique]], that is, he permitted my whole body to be torn with wounds; [[19:10|and I am lost|et pereo]], that is, I die in body: according to that of Isaias, [[Is 57:1|The just perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart|Justus perit, et non est qui recogitet]]. And [[19:10|he hath taken away my hope, as from a tree that is plucked up|quasi avulsæ arbori abstulit spem meam]]. Christ laboured in many ways for the conversion of the Jews, and had at that time a certain hope or expectation of their conversion: which, as regards the greater part of that people, was taken from him when that people became obstinate in its faithlessness. Hence Christ speaks in Isaias: [[Is 49:4|And I said: I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength without cause and in vain|Ego dixi: In vacuum laboravi, sine causa et vane consumpsi fortitudinem meam]].

paras.t: Iratus est contra me furor ejus, et sic me habuit quasi hostem suum. Hoc competit Christo secundum expositionem præcedentis articuli. Ipse equidem fatetur in Psalmo: Super me confirmatus est furor tuus, et omnes fluctus tuos induxisti super me. Unde Isaias scribit: Nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum et percussum a Deo. Christus autem in Scripturis aliquando aliquid loquitur, non secundum quod fuit, sed sicut apparuit, ut est illud: Congregata sunt super me flagella, et ignoravi.
paras.en: [[19:11|His wrath is kindled against me, and he hath counted me as his enemy|Iratus est contra me furor ejus, et sic me habuit quasi hostem suum]]. This fits Christ according to the exposition of the preceding article. He himself indeed confesses in the Psalm: [[Ps 87:8|Thy wrath is strong over me: and all thy waves thou hast brought in upon me|Super me confirmatus est furor tuus, et omnes fluctus tuos induxisti super me]]. Hence Isaias writes: [[Is 53:4|we have thought him as it were a leper, and as one struck by God|Nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum et percussum a Deo]]. But Christ in the Scriptures sometimes says a thing, not according to what was, but as it appeared, as in that saying: [[Ps 34:15|scourges were gathered together upon me, and I knew not|Congregata sunt super me flagella, et ignoravi]].

paras.t: Simul venerunt latrones ejus. De quibus Joannes ait: Cohors, et tribunus, et ministri Judæorum comprehenderunt Jesum. Et fecerunt sibi viam per me, id est, totum corpus meum ictibus atque vulneribus pertransierunt. Obsederunt in gyro tabernaculum, id est corpus meum. Unde et Petrus in secunda sua scribit epistola: Scio quia velox est depositio tabernaculi mei. Hinc Christus ait in Psalmo: Circumdederunt me canes multi; concilium malignantium obsedit me. Et sicut fecerunt corpori Christi vero, ita et corpori ejus mystico, puta Ecclesiæ primitivæ. Latrones quoque sunt invisibiles hostes animarum, fraudulentissimi jugulatores: qui contra Christi famulos veniunt, Ecclesiam obsident; atque in cordibus plurimorum quos tentant, præsertim quos vincunt, sibi efficiunt viam, quia in mentibus succumbentium quasi libere ambulant, dum eos de vitio ad vitium ducunt.
paras.en: [[19:12|His troops have come together|Simul venerunt latrones ejus]] [*latrones*, robbers; the Douay-Rheims has troops]. Of whom John says: [[John 18:12|the band and the tribune and the servants of the Jews took Jesus|Cohors, et tribunus, et ministri Judæorum comprehenderunt Jesum]]. And [[19:12|have made themselves a way by me|fecerunt sibi viam per me]], that is, they went through my whole body with blows and wounds. They [[19:12|have besieged my tabernacle round about|Obsederunt in gyro tabernaculum]], that is, my body. Hence Peter too writes in his second epistle: I know that [[2 Pet 1:14|the laying away of this my tabernacle is at hand|velox est depositio tabernaculi mei]] [Denis has *Scio quia*, I know that, for the Vulgate's *certus quod*, being assured that]. Hence Christ says in the Psalm: [[Ps 21:17|many dogs have encompassed me: the council of the malignant hath besieged me|Circumdederunt me canes multi; concilium malignantium obsedit me]]. And as they did to Christ's true body, so too to his mystical body, namely the primitive Church. The robbers, too, are the invisible enemies of souls, most deceitful cut-throats, who come against the servants of Christ and besiege the Church; and in the hearts of many whom they tempt, especially of those they overcome, they make themselves a way, since they walk as it were freely in the minds of those who give way, while they lead them from vice to vice.

paras.t: Fratres meos longe fecit a me. Tempore enim passionis fugerunt a Christo Apostoli. De quibus post passionem dixit Mariæ Magdalenæ: Vade, dic fratribus meis. Et ad Patrem in Psalmo: Narrabo nomen tuum fratribus meis. Et noti mei quasi alieni recesserunt a me, ceteri scilicet discipuli. Inquilini domus meæ: per quos recte intelliguntur quidam ex gentilibus Christo credentes, sicque ad ejus domum, id est congregationem et familiam, pertinentes; et ancillæ meæ sicut alienum habuerunt me, tempore passionis, quando et multæ feminarum, quæ aliquando Christo crediderant, suggestionibus virorum ab ipso aversæ fuisse creduntur: quamvis omnes mulieres Hebrææ Christi ancillæ possint intelligi, in quantum unius veri Dei cultrices erant, vel esse se affirmabant. Et quasi peregrinus fui in oculis eorum non curantium nec attendentium me.
paras.en: [[19:13|He hath put my brethren far from me|Fratres meos longe fecit a me]]. For at the time of the passion the Apostles fled from Christ[[Matt 26:56||]]. Of them he said after the passion to Mary Magdalene: [[John 20:17|go to my brethren and say to them|Vade, dic fratribus meis]]; and to the Father in the Psalm: [[Ps 21:23|I will declare thy name to my brethren|Narrabo nomen tuum fratribus meis]]. And [[19:13|my acquaintance like strangers have departed from me|noti mei quasi alieni recesserunt a me]], namely the other disciples. [[19:15|They that dwell in my house|Inquilini domus meæ]]: by whom are rightly understood some of the Gentiles who believed in Christ, and so belonged to his house, that is, his congregation and household; [[19:15|and my maidservants have counted me as a stranger|et ancillæ meæ sicut alienum habuerunt me]], at the time of the passion, when also many of the women who had once believed in Christ are thought to have been turned away from him by the suggestions of men: although all the Hebrew women can be understood as Christ's handmaids, inasmuch as they were worshippers of the one true God, or claimed to be. And [[19:15|I have been like an alien in their eyes|quasi peregrinus fui in oculis eorum]], who did not care for me nor heed me.

paras.t: Servum meum vocavi, id est, populum Judæorum, servili timore potius quam filiali amore Deo obsequentem, ad fidem et gratiam invitavi et docui; et non respondit, per obedientiam: quia comparative pauci crediderunt. Unde Apostolus allegat Isaiam, in Christi persona dicentem: Tota die expandi manus meas ad populum non credentem et contradicentem. Ore proprio deprecabar illum. Christus enim nunc blandis, nunc promissoriis sermonibus hortabatur hunc populum ad salutem: et qui ante per Prophetas et alios hoc peregit, tandem in propria persona homo factus hoc fecit, sicut et Isaias prædixit: Erunt oculi tui videntes præceptorem tuum, et aures tuæ audient vocem post terga monentis.
paras.en: [[19:16|I called my servant|Servum meum vocavi]], that is, the Jewish people, who served God with servile fear rather than filial love: I invited them to faith and grace and taught them; [[19:16|and he gave me no answer|et non respondit]] by obedience, since comparatively few believed. Hence the Apostle cites Isaias, speaking in the person of Christ: [[Rom 10:21|All the day long have I spread my hands to a people that believeth not and contradicteth me|Tota die expandi manus meas ad populum non credentem et contradicentem]][[Is 65:2||]]. [[19:16|I entreated him with my own mouth|Ore proprio deprecabar illum]]. For Christ exhorted this people to salvation, now with gentle words, now with promises; and he who before had done this through the Prophets and others at length did it in his own person, made man, as Isaias too foretold: [[Is 30:20|thy eyes shall see thy teacher|Erunt oculi tui videntes præceptorem tuum]], and [[Is 30:21|thy ears shall hear the word of one admonishing thee behind thy back|aures tuæ audient vocem post terga monentis]] [Denis has *vocem*, the voice, for the Vulgate's *verbum*].

paras.t: Præterea, Christus nunc conqueri potest hæc de impiis Christianis: qui fide et nomine, non caritate et actu, inquilini et ancillæ sunt domus, id est Ecclesiæ Christi: attamen peccando ab ipso recedunt, et quasi alienum et peregrinum Christum hic habent, ejus doctrinam non intuendo, ejus præcepta parvi pendendo, mentem ab ipso viliter avertendo. Sed et servum suum, scilicet populum christianum, Christus proprio ore vocavit, vocat, ac deprecatur, ut convertatur atque obediat. Vocat autem nunc, per Scripturas, per angelicam directionem, per occultam inspirationem, per prælatorum ac prædicatorum atque doctorum admonitionem.
paras.en: Further, Christ can now make these complaints of wicked Christians, who in faith and name, though not in charity and deed, are dwellers and handmaids of his house, that is, of the Church of Christ: yet by sinning they depart from him, and here hold Christ as an alien and a stranger, not heeding his doctrine, setting little store by his precepts, basely turning their minds away from him. And Christ has called his servant too, namely the Christian people, with his own mouth, and calls and entreats it, that it may be converted and obey. And he calls now through the Scriptures, through the guidance of the angels, through hidden inspiration, through the admonition of prelates, preachers and doctors.

paras.t: Halitum meum exhorruit uxor mea: id est, Synagoga olim sponsa uxorque mea, me incarnatum ac præsentem ita contempsit, quod mihi nequaquam voluit appropinquare: imo gravis ei exstiti ad videndum, nec voluit me audire. Talis autem aversio solet per halitus exhorrentiam designari. Unde in Exodo filii Israel leguntur dixisse Moysi et Aaron: Fœtere fecistis odorem nostrum coram Pharaone. Fuit autem Synagoga olim sponsa et uxor Christi, sicut modo Ecclesia, de qua fertur in Apocalypsi: Venerunt nuptiæ Agni, et uxor ejus præparavit se. Synagoga vero per suam incredulitatem facta est adultera meretrixque diaboli, ac repudiata a Deo, prout Isaias ait: Quis est hic liber repudii matris vestræ, quo dimisi eam? Et orabam filios uteri mei, id est Judæos, quos practice intelligendo creavi, et sapientia mentis meæ instruxi. Uterus quippe (ut dictum est) pro intellectu seu mente frequenter accipitur, ubi interior animæ proles, quæ est verbum ipsius, concipitur. Unde in Proverbiis Salomon loquitur: Fili, accipe doctrinam meam, quæ tibi pulchra erit quum acceperis eam in ventre tuo. De his filiis Isaias testatur: Filios enutrivi et exaltavi; ipsi autem spreverunt me. Judæos autem (ut dictum est) Christus etiam deprecatorie ad salutem commonuit.
paras.en: [[19:17|My wife hath abhorred my breath|Halitum meum exhorruit uxor mea]]: that is, the Synagogue, once my bride and wife, so despised me when I was incarnate and present that she would by no means come near me: nay, I was grievous to her even to look upon, nor would she hear me. Such aversion is commonly signified by abhorrence of the breath. Hence in Exodus the children of Israel are read to have said to Moses and Aaron: You have [[Ex 5:21|made our savour to stink before Pharao|Fœtere fecistis odorem nostrum coram Pharaone]]. Now the Synagogue was once the bride and wife of Christ, as the Church is now, of which it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 19:7|the marriage of the Lamb is come: and his wife hath prepared herself|Venerunt nuptiæ Agni, et uxor ejus præparavit se]]. But the Synagogue by her unbelief became an adulteress and the devil's harlot, and was put away by God, as Isaias says: [[Is 50:1|What is this bill of the divorce of your mother, with which I have put her away?|Quis est hic liber repudii matris vestræ, quo dimisi eam?]] And [[19:17|I entreated the children of my womb|orabam filios uteri mei]], that is, the Jews, whom I created by practical understanding [that is, the understanding as it directs making and doing, not mere contemplation], and instructed by the wisdom of my mind. For the womb (as has been said) is often taken for the understanding or mind, where the soul's inner offspring, which is its word, is conceived. Hence Salomon speaks in the Proverbs: My son, receive my doctrine[[Prov 22:17||]], [[Prov 22:18|Which shall be beautiful for thee, if thou keep it in thy bowels|quæ tibi pulchra erit quum acceperis eam in ventre tuo]] [the margin gives Prov. xxii, 17, 18; Denis's *Fili, accipe doctrinam meam* is looser than 22:17, *appone autem cor ad doctrinam meam*]. Of these sons Isaias testifies: [[Is 1:2|I have brought up children, and exalted them: but they have despised me|Filios enutrivi et exaltavi; ipsi autem spreverunt me]]. And Christ also admonished the Jews (as has been said) to salvation by entreaty.

paras.t: Stulti quoque despiciebant me: quod de Herodianis et ministris Pilati, ceterisque gentilibus Christum persequentibus opere vel consensu, specialiter accipi potest; vel de vulgo Judæorum indocto, de quo loquitur Jeremias: Et dixi, Forsitan pauperes sunt et stulti, ignorantes viam Domini et judicium Dei sui. Et quum ab eis recessissem, detrahebant mihi: juxta illud Joannis: Murmur multum erat de eo in turba. Quidam enim dicebant, Quia bonus est; alii autem dicebant, Non, sed seducit turbas. Nemo tamen palam loquebatur de illo. Detractio autem mortale peccatum est, valde grave, et gravius furto. Ideo Ecclesiastes dixit: Quomodo si mordeat serpens in silentio, nihil eo minus habet qui occulte detrahit. Justo autem detrahere, prorsus enorme est.
paras.en: [[19:18|Even fools despised me|Stulti quoque despiciebant me]]: this can be taken especially of the Herodians and the servants of Pilate, and the other Gentiles who persecuted Christ by deed or by consent; or of the unlearned common people of the Jews, of whom Jeremias speaks: [[Jer 5:4|I said: Perhaps these are poor and foolish, that know not the way of the Lord, the judgment of their God|Et dixi, Forsitan pauperes sunt et stulti, ignorantes viam Domini et judicium Dei sui]]. [[19:18|And when I was gone from them, they spoke against me|Et quum ab eis recessissem, detrahebant mihi]]: according to that of John: [[John 7:12|there was much murmuring among the multitude concerning him. For some said: He is a good man. And others said: No, but he seduceth the people|Murmur multum erat de eo in turba. Quidam enim dicebant, Quia bonus est; alii autem dicebant, Non, sed seducit turbas]]. [[John 7:13|Yet no man spoke openly of him|Nemo tamen palam loquebatur de illo]]. Now detraction [that is, backbiting: blackening another's good name behind his back] is a mortal sin, very grave, and graver than theft. Therefore Ecclesiastes said: [[Eccles 10:11|If a serpent bite in silence, he is nothing better that backbiteth secretly|Quomodo si mordeat serpens in silentio, nihil eo minus habet qui occulte detrahit]]. But to speak against a just man is altogether monstrous.

paras.t: Abominati sunt me quondam consiliarii mei, videlicet sacerdotes, Scribæ et Pharisæi: qui consiliarii Dei seu Christi fuerunt, quasi ad ipsum pertinentes, non quasi ei consilium impendentes, sed populo ejus. Quemadmodum in Genesi filii Heth loquuntur ad Abraham, Princeps Dei es apud nos: ubi alia translatio habet, Rex Dei es apud nos. Et quem maxime diligebam, aversatus est me. Posset hoc exponi de Juda proditore, quem Christus maxime, id est valde multum, dilexit, quantum ad amicitiæ signa, et beneficia gratiæ gratis datæ. Nam fecit eum Apostolum suum, procuratoremque: et forte ad tempus fuit in caritate et gratia. Denique princeps Apostolorum ore tenus cum anathematizatione ac juramento Christum negavit. Insuper ordo pontificalis præ ceteris a Deo electus, Christum specialiter noscitur persecutus.
paras.en: [[19:19|They that were sometime my counsellors, have abhorred me|Abominati sunt me quondam consiliarii mei]], namely the priests, Scribes and Pharisees: who were counsellors of God, or of Christ, as belonging to him, not as giving counsel to him, but to his people. Just as in Genesis the children of Heth say to Abraham, [[Gen 23:6|thou art a prince of God among us|Princeps Dei es apud nos]]: where another translation has, Thou art a king of God among us. [[19:19|And he whom I loved most is turned against me|Et quem maxime diligebam, aversatus est me]]. This might be explained of Judas the traitor, whom Christ loved most, that is, very greatly, as regards the tokens of friendship and the gifts of grace freely given [*gratia gratis data*: graces given for the good of others, such as office or the power of miracles, which do not of themselves make the receiver holy]. For he made him his Apostle, and his purse-bearer[[John 12:6||]][[John 13:29||]]; and perhaps for a time he was in charity and grace. Then too the prince of the Apostles denied Christ with his lips, with cursing and an oath[[Mark 14:71||]]. Moreover the order of the high priests, chosen by God before the rest, is known to have persecuted Christ in a special way.

paras.t: Pelli meæ, consumptis carnibus, adhæsit os meum. Tempore passionis, sanguine Christi exhausto, et corpore vulneribus dilacerato, violentissimeque distento, caro ejus magna ex parte attenuata est, ita ut ossa viderentur pelli hærere, quia dilapsa dispersaque fuit caro ejus tenerrima. Et derelicta sunt tantummodo labia circa dentes meos, id est, ceteris membris meis suo officio quodammodo destitutis, solius mihi linguæ usus remansit tempore crucifixionis. Nam et Christus voce magna exclamans, tradidit spiritum: quod supernaturale fuisse considerans ipse centurio, Vere, inquit, hic homo Filius Dei fuit.
paras.en: [[19:20|The flesh being consumed, my bone hath cleaved to my skin|Pelli meæ, consumptis carnibus, adhæsit os meum]]. In the time of the passion, when Christ's blood was drained, and his body torn with wounds and most violently stretched, his flesh was in great part wasted away, so that the bones seemed to cleave to the skin, because his most tender flesh had fallen away and was spent. [[19:20|And nothing but lips are left about my teeth|Et derelicta sunt tantummodo labia circa dentes meos]], that is, my other members being in a manner deprived of their office, the use of my tongue alone remained to me in the time of the crucifixion. For Christ too, crying out with a loud voice, gave up the ghost[[Matt 27:50||]] [the margin reads Matth. xxvi, 90, evidently for xxvii, 50]: and the centurion himself, considering that this was beyond nature, said: [[Mark 15:39|Indeed|Vere]], he said, [[Mark 15:39|this man was the son of God|hic homo Filius Dei fuit]].

paras.t: Miseremini mei, miseremini mei, saltem vos, amici mei. Christus sibi condolere suos optavit, quemadmodum naturale censetur afflictis. Propter quod ait in Psalmo: Sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit: et qui consolaretur, et non inveni. Præterea per amicos ejus, intelligi possunt omnes qui adfuerunt Judæi: qui licet pro majori parte fuerint ejus inimici, tamen amici vocantur, quoniam Christus eos amavit, et quoniam quidam eorum prædestinati fuerunt. Sicque amici tunc erant non secundum præsentem justitiam, sed secundum prædestinationem æternam, qui postea sunt conversi: quibus passione instante prædixit, Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum. Judæis quoque Christus multa specialia beneficia erogavit: ideo præ ceteris ejus dicebantur amici. Unde eorum ingratitudo, perfidia, et persecutio sibi molestior fuit. Itaque ait: Miseremini mei, etc., tanquam dicat: Gentilibus me tam dire cædentibus, saltem vos, Judæi, populus propter quem veni, condolete. Nihilo minus, per amicos, intelligi possunt Judæi tunc quodammodo increduli, puta discipuli, qui sive absentes, sive præsentes, Christo intime compatiebantur. Quia manus Domini tetigit me. Deo enim permittente occisus est Christus. Imo Deus se id fecisse testatur per Isaiam: Propter scelus, inquiens, populi mei percussi eum. In Actis quoque loquitur Petrus: Deus qui prædixit per os omnium Prophetarum pati Christum suum, implevit sic.
paras.en: [[19:21|Have pity on me, have pity on me, at least you my friends|Miseremini mei, miseremini mei, saltem vos, amici mei]]. Christ wished his own to grieve with him, as is held natural for the afflicted. Wherefore he says in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:21|I looked for one that would grieve together with me, but there was none: and for one that would comfort me, and I found none|Sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit: et qui consolaretur, et non inveni]]. Further, by his friends can be understood all the Jews who were present: who, though for the most part they were his enemies, are yet called friends, because Christ loved them, and because some of them were predestined. And so those who were afterwards converted were friends at that time, not according to present justice, but according to eternal predestination: to whom, as the passion drew near, he foretold: [[John 8:28|When you shall have lifted up, the Son of man, then shall you know that I am he|Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum]]. Christ also bestowed many special benefits on the Jews: therefore before the rest they were called his friends. Hence their ingratitude, faithlessness and persecution were the more grievous to him. And so he says: [[19:21|Have pity on me|Miseremini mei]], etc., as though to say: While the Gentiles beat me so cruelly, at least you, Jews, the people for whose sake I came, grieve with me. Nevertheless, by the friends can be understood Jews who were then in a manner unbelieving, the disciples for example, who, whether absent or present, suffered inwardly with Christ. [[19:21|Because the hand of the Lord hath touched me|Quia manus Domini tetigit me]]. For it was by God's permission that Christ was slain. Indeed God bears witness through Isaias that he did it himself: [[Is 53:8|For the wickedness|Propter scelus]], he says, [[Is 53:8|of my people have I struck him|populi mei percussi eum]]. In the Acts also Peter says: [[Acts 3:18|God before had shewed by the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled|Deus qui prædixit per os omnium Prophetarum pati Christum suum, implevit sic]].

paras.t: Crudelibus vero incredulisque Judæis loquitur consequenter: Quare persequimini me sicut Deus? Hoc secundum præcedentis articuli elucidationem competit Christo, qui etiam ait Deum se persequi permissive: et quia per Filii sui unigeniti persecutionem et mortem, præordinavit genus salvare humanum; hinc Filius loquitur Patri in Psalmo: Quem tu percussisti, persecuti sunt. Et carnibus meis saturamini? Hoc rursus secundum præhabitam expositionem maxime competit Christo, de cujus amarissimis pœnis crudelissimi persecutores vehementissime gestiebant.
paras.en: Next he speaks to the cruel and unbelieving Jews: [[19:22|Why do you persecute me as God|Quare persequimini me sicut Deus]]? According to the explanation in the preceding article this fits Christ, who also says that God persecutes him, by permitting it: and because God foreordained to save the human race through the persecution and death of his only-begotten Son, the Son therefore says to the Father in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:27|they have persecuted him whom thou hast smitten|Quem tu percussisti, persecuti sunt]]. [[19:22|And glut yourselves with my flesh|Et carnibus meis saturamini]]? This too, according to the exposition already given, fits Christ above all, over whose most bitter pains his most cruel persecutors exulted most vehemently.

paras.t: Quis mihi tribuat ut scribantur sermones mei? Christus utique verba sua jam in cruce et tempore passionis, et ante prolata sciens saluberrima esse, optavit ea ad mundi instructionem scribi tam in libris, quam in hominum cordibus: quod etiam fiendum certissime noverat. Ideo subditur: Quis mihi det ut exarentur in libro, id est corde Judæorum, ob quorum instructionem Christus specialiter missum se perhibet, stylo ferreo, id est profunda et forti inscriptione, prædicatione, seu illuminatione, per quam verba divina menti imprimuntur humanæ; aut in plumbi lamina: per quam intelligitur cor gravium personarum, quæ religiosiores videntur. Quod Christus adjunxit, quia a communi populo Judæorum noverat sua verba spernenda, ideo cupiebat ut saltem ab eis reciperentur, qui majoris probitatis æstimabantur: quod et partim completum est, quia, ut Acta habent, Multa turba sacerdotum obediebat fidei. Sed quoniam major pars plebis hujusmodi mansit incredula, optavit Salvator ut converteretur gentilitas. Propter quod subditur, vel certe sculpantur in silice, id est duro gentilium corde: de quibus dixit Salvator, Alias oves habeo qui non sunt de hoc ovili, et illas oportet me adducere. Denique, de spirituali hac inscriptione, qua evangelica lex in cordibus scripta est electorum, allegat Apostolus ad Hebræos testimonium Jeremiæ, Deum inducens dicentem: Dabo leges meas in mentes eorum, et in corde eorum superscribam eas. Sequentia autem verba non proprie congruunt Christo, qui non in novissimo die resurget, sed die tertio resurrexit.
paras.en: [[19:23|Who will grant me that my words may be written|Quis mihi tribuat ut scribantur sermones mei]]? Christ, knowing that the words he spoke on the cross and in the time of the passion, and before it, were most wholesome, wished them to be written for the instruction of the world, as much in books as in the hearts of men: and he knew most certainly that this would be done. Therefore it is added: [[19:23|who will grant me that they may be marked down in a book|Quis mihi det ut exarentur in libro]], that is, in the heart of the Jews, for whose instruction Christ declares that he was especially sent, [[19:24|With an iron pen|stylo ferreo]], that is, by a deep and strong inscription, preaching, or enlightening, by which the divine words are pressed upon the human mind; [[19:24|and in a plate of lead|aut in plumbi lamina]]: by which is understood the heart of grave persons, who seem more religious. Christ added this because he knew that his words would be spurned by the common people of the Jews, and therefore he desired that they might at least be received by those who were reckoned of greater uprightness: and this was in part fulfilled, since, as the Acts have it, [[Acts 6:7|A great multitude also of the priests obeyed the faith|Multa turba sacerdotum obediebat fidei]]. But since the greater part of these common people remained unbelieving, the Saviour wished the Gentiles to be converted. Wherefore it is added, [[19:24|or else be graven with an instrument in flint stone|vel certe sculpantur in silice]] [Denis reads *vel certe*, "or surely", where the Vulgate has *vel celte*, "or with a chisel"; the Douay-Rheims "with an instrument" follows *celte*], that is, in the hard heart of the Gentiles: of whom the Saviour said, [[John 10:16|other sheep I have that are not of this fold: them also I must bring|Alias oves habeo qui non sunt de hoc ovili, et illas oportet me adducere]]. Lastly, of this spiritual inscription, by which the law of the Gospel is written in the hearts of the elect, the Apostle in the Epistle to the Hebrews brings forward the testimony of Jeremias, presenting God as saying: [[Heb 8:10|I will give my laws into their mind: and in their heart will I write them|Dabo leges meas in mentes eorum, et in corde eorum superscribam eas]][[Heb 10:16||]][[Jer 31:33||]]. But the words that follow do not properly fit Christ, who will not rise [[19:25|in the last day|in novissimo die]], but rose again on the third day.

paras.t: Insuper ex præinductis faciliter reor patere, qualiter verba hujus capituli de quocumque gravissime afflicto ac justo, per Job figurato, et Christi imitatore, queant exponi: quod causa vitandæ prolixitatis non prosequor; sed circa pleniorem tractationem verborum hujus capituli quæ pro lectione dicuntur in Officio defunctorum, paululum immorabor.
paras.en: Moreover I think it readily appears from what has been brought forward how the words of this chapter can be explained of any just man who is most grievously afflicted, prefigured by Job, and an imitator of Christ: which, to avoid prolixity, I do not pursue; but I shall dwell a little on a fuller treatment of those words of this chapter which are said as a lesson in the Office of the Dead.

paras.t: Pelli meæ, consumptis carnibus, adhæsit os meum, etc. Si quis tantam inciderit infirmitatem, aut tantam fecerit abstinentiam, ut caro ejus pro magna parte cernatur consumpta, ita ut dicere valeat cum Psalmista: Ossa mea sicut cremium aruerunt; percussus sum ut fœnum; a voce gemitus mei adhæsit os meum carni meæ, id est pelli, secundum Hieronymum: talis verba hæc Job dicere potest, qui amicorum petit suffragium, Miseremini mei, miseremini mei, saltem vos, amici mei. Tempore etenim adversitatis et necessitatis, præcipue amicitia est monstranda. Ideo dicit Ecclesiasticus: Si possides amicum, in tentatione posside eum, et ne facile credas ei te ipsum. Est enim amicus secundum tempus suum, et non permanet in die tribulationis. Itemque: Non te pigeat visitare infirmum: ex his enim in dilectione firmaberis. Et alibi scriptum est: Frater in angustiis comprobatur. Talibus ergo misereamur interiori compassione, et subveniamus pro posse, orando, consolando, ministrando, de necessariis providendo. Quia manus Domini tetigit me, paternaliter in hac vita castigando, quemadmodum legitur: Castigans castigavit me Dominus. Interdum autem manus Domini tangit nos in spiritualibus donis, illa dispensatorie suspendendo, aut juste tollendo: tuncque majori sollicitudine atque custodia indigemus, et aliorum spirituale subsidium implorare debemus, ne in mente gravius vulneremur, sed statim curemur seu reparemur.
paras.en: [[19:20|The flesh being consumed, my bone hath cleaved to my skin|Pelli meæ, consumptis carnibus, adhæsit os meum]], etc. If anyone has fallen into so great an infirmity, or has practised so great an abstinence, that his flesh is seen to be in great part consumed, so that he can say with the Psalmist: [[Ps 101:4|my bones are grown dry like fuel for the fire|Ossa mea sicut cremium aruerunt]]; [[Ps 101:5|I am smitten as grass|percussus sum ut fœnum]]; [[Ps 101:6|Through the voice of my groaning, my bone hath cleaved to my flesh|a voce gemitus mei adhæsit os meum carni meæ]], that is, to the skin, according to Jerome: such a one can say these words of Job, who begs the help of his friends, [[19:21|Have pity on me, have pity on me, at least you my friends|Miseremini mei, miseremini mei, saltem vos, amici mei]]. For in the time of adversity and need above all friendship is to be shown. Therefore Ecclesiasticus says: [[Ecclus 6:7|If thou wouldst get a friend, try him before thou takest him, and do not credit him easily|Si possides amicum, in tentatione posside eum, et ne facile credas ei te ipsum]] [Denis's text reads, literally: If thou possessest a friend, possess him in temptation, and do not easily entrust thyself to him]. [[Ecclus 6:8|For there is a friend for his own occasion, and he will not abide in the day of thy trouble|Est enim amicus secundum tempus suum, et non permanet in die tribulationis]]. And again: [[Ecclus 7:39|Be not slow to visit the sick: for by these things thou shalt be confirmed in love|Non te pigeat visitare infirmum: ex his enim in dilectione firmaberis]]. And elsewhere it is written: [[Prov 17:17|a brother is proved in distress|Frater in angustiis comprobatur]]. Let us therefore have pity on such people with inward compassion, and help them as far as we can, by praying, consoling, serving, and providing what they need. [[19:21|Because the hand of the Lord hath touched me|Quia manus Domini tetigit me]], chastising me as a father in this life, as we read: [[Ps 117:18|The Lord chastising hath chastised me|Castigans castigavit me Dominus]]. But sometimes the hand of the Lord touches us in our spiritual gifts, suspending them by dispensation, or justly taking them away: and then we need greater care and watchfulness, and ought to implore the spiritual help of others, lest we be more grievously wounded in mind, but may at once be healed or restored.

paras.t: Quare persequimini me sicut Deus, et carnibus meis saturamini? Hoc, juxta expositionem præhabitam, duris incompassivisque dicitur: de quibus in Proverbiorum libro fertur, Viscera impiorum crudelia. Tales autem, iniqui sunt vitiosique valde. Unde in Proverbiis legitur: Qui despicit amicum suum, indigens corde est. Benefacit animæ suæ vir misericors; qui autem crudelis est, et propinquos abjicit. Tales attendant et paveant illud Jacobi: Judicium sine misericordia illi, qui non fecerit misericordiam.
paras.en: [[19:22|Why do you persecute me as God, and glut yourselves with my flesh?|Quare persequimini me sicut Deus, et carnibus meis saturamini?]] According to the exposition already given, this is said to the hard and pitiless: of whom it is said in the book of Proverbs, [[Prov 12:10|the bowels of the wicked are cruel|Viscera impiorum crudelia]]. Such men are very wicked and full of vice. Hence we read in Proverbs: [[Prov 11:12|He that despiseth his friend, is mean of heart|Qui despicit amicum suum, indigens corde est]]. [[Prov 11:17|A merciful man doth good to his own soul: but he that is cruel casteth off even his own kindred|Benefacit animæ suæ vir misericors; qui autem crudelis est, et propinquos abjicit]]. Let such men heed and fear that saying of James: [[Jas 2:13|judgment without mercy to him that hath not done mercy|Judicium sine misericordia illi, qui non fecerit misericordiam]].

paras.t: Quis mihi tribuat ut scribantur sermones mei? etc. Qui ex gratia sibi collata profert sententiosa atque utilia, merito ex caritate cupit ea ad aliorum profectum commendari memoriæ et scripturæ, præsertim quum in Ecclesiastico scriptum sit: Sapientia absconsa et thesaurus invisus, quæ utilitas in utrisque?
paras.en: [[19:23|Who will grant me that my words may be written?|Quis mihi tribuat ut scribantur sermones mei?]] etc. He who, from the grace bestowed on him, utters weighty and profitable sayings, rightly desires out of charity that they be committed to memory and to writing for the profit of others, especially since it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 20:32|Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is not seen: what profit is there in them both?|Sapientia absconsa et thesaurus invisus, quæ utilitas in utrisque?]]

paras.t: Scio enim quod Redemptor meus vivit: quemadmodum ad Romanos dicit Apostolus, Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur: qui secundum divinitatem æternaliter et incommutabiliter est vivens et vita. Hunc Redemptorem tanto amplius diligere debemus, quo in se ipso est melior, et quo a pœna majori nos liberavit, ad majora quoque bona perduxit; quo item hoc amorosius, pretiosius ac laboriosius fecit. Quum igitur ab æterna nos damnatione, pœna et morte redemerit, gratiam et gloriam nobis meruerit, et proprii sanguinis effusione cum amarissima passione hoc egerit, constat quod eum toto corde in omnibus et super omnia semper amare, timere, honorare incomparabiliter obligemur: quod nisi fecerimus, ingratissimi atque vilissimi canes probabimur. Et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum, etc. Verba hæc satis exposita sunt. Omnes quoque in die judicii videbunt Christum Deum et judicem in forma humana. Beati vero ejus tunc divinitatem etiam intuebuntur. Præterea verba hæc vigilantissime ponderare ac penetrare debemus, felicemque resurrectionem cordialissime desiderare, et pro ea efficaciter laborare: sed et metuendissimum Dei judicium tota mente vereri; et quæ tunc futura sunt, tanquam præsentia oculis fidei quotidie intueri.
paras.en: [[19:25|For I know that my Redeemer liveth|Scio enim quod Redemptor meus vivit]]: as the Apostle says to the Romans, [[Rom 6:9|Christ, rising again from the dead, dieth now no more|Christus resurgens ex mortuis, jam non moritur]]: who according to his divinity is eternally and unchangeably living, and life itself. We ought to love this Redeemer all the more, the better he is in himself, and the greater the punishment from which he has freed us, and the greater the goods to which he has brought us; and again, the more lovingly, the more preciously and the more laboriously he did it. Since, then, he has redeemed us from eternal damnation, punishment and death, has merited grace and glory for us, and has done this by the shedding of his own blood with a most bitter passion, it is plain that we are bound beyond compare always to love, fear and honour him with our whole heart, in all things and above all things: and unless we do so, we shall prove ourselves most ungrateful and most vile dogs. [[19:25|And in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|Et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum]], etc. These words have been explained well enough. All too, on the day of judgment, will see Christ, God and judge, in human form; but his blessed will then behold his divinity as well. Further, we ought to weigh and search into these words most watchfully, to desire a happy resurrection with all our heart, and to labour for it effectually: and also to dread God's most fearful judgment with our whole mind; and daily to look with the eyes of faith on the things that will then be, as though they were present.

paras.t: Postremo tangendum, quomodo lectio ista conveniat animæ in purgatorio constitutæ. Talis siquidem anima si languore gravi et longo separata fuit a corpore, dicere potest de corpore quod habebat: Pelli meæ, etc. Quod ait ad provocandam Dei clementiam, dum propriam commemorat calamitatem. Insuper anima talis gravissime dolens, nec tamen juvare se valens, amicorum precatur suffragia: Miseremini mei, miseremini mei. Repetitio verbi, indicium est intensi affectus, gravissimique doloris.
