Saltem vos, amici mei, videlicet propinqui, familiares, amatores, et quibus aliquando benefeci, aut bona quæ habui possidetis atque consumitis. Unde specialis vobis ratio miserendi est mihi, caritate et justitia exigentibus istud. Itaque, miseremini mei, pro me orando, eleemosynas tribuendo, jejunando, celebrando, aut cetera virtutum opera pro me satisfactoria exercendo. Sed, heu! in hoc multi viventium negligentes sunt vehementer, dum nec filii parentibus, nec beneficiati benefactoribus, nec propinqui cognatis, nec amici amicis, nec in fiducia habiti commendatis, defunctis (ut dignum est) præfatis modis jam miserentur: imo parum attendunt, in quantis illi sint pœnis; quam affectuose sibi postulent subveniri; quantum etiam teneantur illis succurrere. Noverint hi quia sic fiet sibi, quomodo faciunt aliis. Quia manus Domini tetigit me, id est pœnis istis affligit.
paras.en: Lastly it must be touched on how this lesson fits a soul placed in purgatory. For such a soul, if it was parted from the body by a long and grave illness, can say of the body it had: [[19:20|my bone hath cleaved to my skin|Pelli meæ]], etc. And it says this to call forth God's clemency, while it recalls its own calamity. Moreover such a soul, grieving most grievously and yet unable to help itself, begs the help of its friends: [[19:21|Have pity on me, have pity on me|Miseremini mei, miseremini mei]]. The repetition of the word is a sign of intense affection and of very grievous pain. [[19:21|At least you my friends|Saltem vos, amici mei]], namely kinsmen, members of my household, those who loved me, and those to whom I once did good, or who possess and use up the goods I had. Hence you have a special reason to pity me, charity and justice requiring it. Therefore have pity on me, by praying for me, giving alms, fasting, celebrating Mass, or performing the other works of virtue that make satisfaction for me [that is, that pay the debt of temporal punishment still owed for forgiven sins]. But alas! in this many of the living are exceedingly negligent, since neither children for their parents, nor those who have received benefits for their benefactors, nor kinsmen for their relatives, nor friends for their friends, nor those who were trusted for those committed to them, now take pity on the dead in the ways mentioned (as is fitting): rather they pay little heed to how great the pains are in which those souls lie, how earnestly they ask to be helped, and how much they themselves are bound to come to their aid. Let these know that it will be done to them as they do to others[[Luke 6:38||]]. [[19:21|Because the hand of the Lord hath touched me|Quia manus Domini tetigit me]], that is, afflicts me with these pains.

paras.t: Quare persequimini me sicut Deus? Hoc anima dicit adversus eos, qui occasio sunt quod pœna sua in purgatorii loco augetur, qui scilicet animæ culpas sequuntur, aut mala ejus incaute commemorant: quod, secundum Gregorium, vicissim vergit in pœnarum animæ incrementum. Et carnibus meis, id est carnalibus opibus seu operibus, saturamini, utendo meis, nec tamen digne mihi subvenientes. In quo et sacerdotes et canonici religiosique ceteri inveniuntur maxime ac damnabiliter defectuosi, non orando ac satisfaciendo pro his, quorum eleemosynis utuntur aut sustentantur, sicut caritas æquitasque requirunt. Contra quos S. Bernardus terribiliter scribit, quia sacrilegi sunt, bonis Ecclesiæ abutendo, et de eleemosynis pauperum delicate se nutriendo, pretiose, curiose atque superbe vestiendo, ac sceleratissime superbiendo. Itaque pro benefactoribus nostris vivis ac mortuis jugiter efficaciterque oremus, grati simus; et ita vivamus, ut pro nobis ipsis ac aliis idonei deprecatores inveniamur.
paras.en: [[19:22|Why do you persecute me as God|Quare persequimini me sicut Deus]]? The soul says this against those who are the occasion of its pain being increased in the place of purgatory: namely those who follow the soul's faults, or heedlessly speak of its evil deeds; which, according to Gregory, in turn tends to increase the soul's pains. It goes on: [[19:22|and glut yourselves|saturamini]] [[19:22|with my flesh|Et carnibus meis]], that is, with my fleshly wealth or works, by using what is mine, and yet not helping me as is fitting. In this priests and canons and other religious are found most of all, and damnably, wanting: not praying and making satisfaction for those on whose alms they live or are kept, as charity and equity require. Against them St Bernard writes terribly, that they are sacrilegious, abusing the goods of the Church, feeding themselves delicately on the alms of the poor, dressing richly, curiously and proudly, and being most wickedly proud. Let us therefore pray continually and effectually for our benefactors living and dead, and be grateful; and let us so live as to be found fit intercessors for ourselves and for others.

paras.t: Quis mihi tribuat ut scribantur sermones mei, etc. Verba equidem animæ talis, tam dolorosa sunt, ipsaque anima taliter angustiatur, quod verba sua cupit scribi, et auxiliari valentibus intimari, ut et ceteri hæc scientes, pœnas has caveant, ac pro ipsa exorent. Scio enim quod Redemptor meus vivit, id est, ideo cupio mihi subveniri, quoniam scio me redimendam, certissime præstolans resurrectionem beatam, sciensque Christum salvatorem meum in cœlis regnantem; et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum ego spiritus rationalis, quando corpus intrabo, informabo, vivificabo ac erigam; sicque cum illo de terra ad judicii locum consurgam: sicut per Joelem Deus prædixit, Consurgant et ascendant gentes in vallem Josaphat, quia ibi sedebo ut judicem omnes gentes in circuitu. Ceterorum verborum lectionis hujus expositio non variatur, sed ex præcedenti patet articulo.
paras.en: [[19:23|Who will grant me that my words may be written|Quis mihi tribuat ut scribantur sermones mei]], etc. The words of such a soul are so sorrowful, and the soul itself is in such anguish, that it desires its words to be written, and made known to those able to help, so that others too, knowing these things, may beware of these pains, and may pray for it. [[19:25|For I know that my Redeemer liveth|Scio enim quod Redemptor meus vivit]], that is: I desire to be helped for this reason, that I know I am to be redeemed, most surely awaiting a blessed resurrection, and knowing that Christ my Saviour reigns in heaven; [[19:25|and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum]], I the rational spirit, when I shall enter the body, inform it [that is, be its form, the principle that makes it a living human body], quicken and raise it; and so with it I shall rise from the earth to the place of judgment: as God foretold through Joel, [[Joel 3:12|Let them arise, and let the nations come up into the valley of Josaphat: for there I will sit to judge all nations round about|Consurgant et ascendant gentes in vallem Josaphat, quia ibi sedebo ut judicem omnes gentes in circuitu]]. The explanation of the other words of this lesson does not change, but is plain from the preceding article.

paras.t: Quod vero in fine capituli legitur, Quare ergo nunc dicitis, Persequamur eum, et radicem verbi inveniamus contra eum? potest esse verbum Christi contra Judæos, qui se ad ejus persecutionem mutuo hortabantur, multipliciterque inter se contulerunt, qualem adversus eum accusationem proponerent. Potest demum esse verbum cujuslibet justi contra impios persecutores. Cetera patent.
paras.en: But what is read at the end of the chapter, [[19:28|Why then do you say now: Let us persecute him, and let us find occasion of word against him?|Quare ergo nunc dicitis, Persequamur eum, et radicem verbi inveniamus contra eum?]] [*radicem verbi*, literally "the root of a word"], can be a word of Christ against the Jews, who urged one another on to persecute him, and conferred among themselves in many ways over what accusation to bring against him. It can also be the word of any just man against wicked persecutors. The rest is plain.

20.title: Declaratio litteralis capituli vicesimi: Respondens autem Sophar Naamathites, dixit.
20.title_en: Literal exposition of the twentieth chapter: Then Sophar the Naamathite answered, and said.

paras.t: Respondens autem Sophar Naamathites, dixit: Idcirco, propter ea quæ dixisti, o Job, cogitationes meæ variæ succedunt sibi, id est, diversa considero, nunc pensando rationes pro tuæ positionis defensione valentes, nunc eas quæ ad contrarium videntur conferre, et meam positionem firmare; et mens in diversa rapitur, id est, intellectus meus in diversa perpendenda ac discutienda defigitur: ut moris est disputantibus, quando nutare incipiunt et dubitare quid verius sit. Doctrinam qua me arguis, id est, reprehendis tanquam male sentientem de providentia Dei, dum dico hominem non flagellari a Deo nisi pro suis peccatis, audiam, non mox eam cum aspernatione abjiciendo, sed quid veri in ea sit, diligentius investigando; et spiritus intelligentiæ meæ, id est spiritus per quem intelligo, scilicet anima ut intellectiva, respondebit mihi, id est, intus mihi ostendet, ac indicabit in consistorio mentis meæ quod verum est: quia per intellectus investigationem veritas invenitur.
paras.en: [[20:1|Then Sophar the Naamathite answered, and said|Respondens autem Sophar Naamathites, dixit]]: [[20:2|Therefore|Idcirco]], because of the things thou hast said, O Job, [[20:2|various thoughts succeed one another in me|cogitationes meæ variæ succedunt sibi]], that is, I consider different things, weighing now the reasons that avail for the defence of thy position, now those that seem to tell for the contrary and to confirm my own position; [[20:2|and my mind is hurried away to different things|et mens in diversa rapitur]], that is, my understanding is fixed on weighing and discussing different things, as is the way with disputants when they begin to waver and to doubt which is the truer. [[20:3|The doctrine with which thou reprovest me|Doctrinam qua me arguis]], that is, with which thou rebukest me as one who thinks ill of the providence of God, when I say that man is not scourged by God except for his own sins, [[20:3|I will hear|audiam]]: not casting it away at once with contempt, but searching out more diligently what truth there is in it; [[20:3|and the spirit of my understanding|et spiritus intelligentiæ meæ]], that is, the spirit by which I understand, namely the soul as intellective, [[20:3|shall answer for me|respondebit mihi]], that is, shall show me inwardly and declare in the council chamber of my mind what is true: for truth is found by the searching of the understanding.

paras.t: Hoc scio, quod subdo, videlicet quod a principio temporis ex quo positus est homo super terram, id est ab exordio constitutionis generis humani, laus impiorum brevis sit, id est, celebris fama eorum cito pertransit, et paulo post diffamantur, quum non vera, sed apparens bonitas virtutis in eis sit, cujus falsitas cito consideratur atque patescit; et gaudium hypocritæ ad instar puncti, id est, nullius est reputationis sive durationis, præsertim respectu veri spiritualisque gaudii, et quoad futuri sæculi æternitatem: non enim vero ac stabili innititur fundamento, sed caduco, vano atque fallaci. Unde in Proverbiis scriptum est: Iter impiorum decipiet eos. In Isaia quoque dicitur impio: Veniet super te malum atque calamitas, et nescies ortum eorum; veniet super te miseria repente.
paras.en: [[20:4|This I know|Hoc scio]], namely what I now add: that [[20:4|from the beginning|a principio]] of time, [[20:4|since man was placed upon the earth|ex quo positus est homo super terram]], that is, from the first founding of the human race, [[20:5|the praise of the wicked is short|laus impiorum brevis sit]], that is, their famous name quickly passes away, and a little later they are defamed, since there is in them not true but only seeming goodness of virtue, whose falseness is soon noticed and comes to light; [[20:5|and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment|et gaudium hypocritæ ad instar puncti]] [literally “like a point”], that is, it is of no account or duration, above all in respect of true and spiritual joy, and as regards the eternity of the world to come: for it rests not on a true and stable foundation, but on one that is perishable, vain and deceitful. Hence it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 12:26|the way of the wicked shall deceive them|Iter impiorum decipiet eos]]. In Isaias also it is said to the wicked man: [[Is 47:11|Evil shall come upon thee|Veniet super te malum]], and calamity, [[Is 47:11|and thou shalt not know the rising|et nescies ortum]] of them; [[Is 47:11|misery shall come upon thee suddenly|veniet super te miseria repente]].

paras.t: Si ascenderit usque ad cœlum superbia ejus, id est, quantumlibet in vita hac prosperetur ac elevetur, etiamsi cœlestibus ac divinis se reputet parem, ut hi qui in vita ista se adorari fecerunt; et caput ejus nubes tetigerit, id est, ambitiosa mens ejus præ aliis sublimiter valde se erigat, Sanctisque, qui nubes vocantur, se præsumptuose æqualem existimet; quasi sterquilinium in fine perdetur, id est, in morte subito deprimetur, atque ut vilissimum cadaver a Deo spernetur, æternaliterque damnabitur. Sic et Psalmista decantat: Vidi impium superexaltatum et elevatum sicut cedros Libani. Et transivi, et ecce non erat; et quæsivi eum, et non est inventus locus ejus. Hinc primo Machabæorum libro inducitur: Gloria peccatoris, stercus et vermis. Hodie extollitur, et cras non invenitur: quia conversus est in terram suam, et cogitatio ejus periit. In visione quoque Abdiæ Dominus comminatur superbo: Si exaltatus fueris ut aquila, et si inter sidera posueris nidum tuum, inde detraham te, dicit Dominus. Et qui eum viderant in prosperitate, sublimitate et gloria, dicent, cognita repentina ejus dejectione: Ubi est? quasi dicant mirando: O quam cito defecit et periit ipse cum omni apparentia sua!
paras.en: [[20:6|If his pride mount up even to heaven|Si ascenderit usque ad cœlum superbia ejus]], that is, however much he may prosper and be raised up in this life, even if he think himself equal to heavenly and divine beings, like those who in this life had themselves worshipped; [[20:6|and his head touch the clouds|et caput ejus nubes tetigerit]], that is, though his ambitious mind lift itself up very high above others, and presumptuously think itself equal to the Saints, who are called clouds: [[20:7|In the end he shall be destroyed like a dunghill|quasi sterquilinium in fine perdetur]], that is, in death he shall be suddenly cast down, and be spurned by God like the vilest carcass, and be damned eternally. So the Psalmist also sings: [[Ps 36:35|I have seen the wicked highly exalted, and lifted up like the cedars of Libanus|Vidi impium superexaltatum et elevatum sicut cedros Libani]]. [[Ps 36:36|And I passed by, and lo, he was not: and I sought him and his place was not found|Et transivi, et ecce non erat; et quæsivi eum, et non est inventus locus ejus]]. Hence it is brought in in the first book of Machabees: The glory of the sinner [[1 Mach 2:62|is dung and worms|stercus et vermis]]. [[1 Mach 2:63|Today he is lifted up, and tomorrow he shall not be found, because he is returned into his earth and his thought is come to nothing|Hodie extollitur, et cras non invenitur: quia conversus est in terram suam, et cogitatio ejus periit]]. In the vision of Abdias, too, the Lord threatens the proud man: [[Abd 1:4|Though thou be exalted as an eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars: thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord|Si exaltatus fueris ut aquila, et si inter sidera posueris nidum tuum, inde detraham te, dicit Dominus]]. [[20:7|And they that had seen him|Et qui eum viderant]] in prosperity, in loftiness and in glory [[20:7|shall say|dicent]], when they learn of his sudden overthrow: [[20:7|Where is he?|Ubi est?]] as if to say in wonder: O how quickly he has failed and perished, with all his show!

paras.t: Velut somnium avolans, id est a mente per oblivionem cito recedens, non invenietur in pristina vita et gloria; transiet sicut visio nocturna, quæ momentanea esse solet: sic ipse de vita tolletur et disperibit, quasi hic nunquam fuisset. Sic et in Psalmis cantatur: Dejecisti eos dum allevarentur. Quomodo facti sunt in desolationem? Subito defecerunt, perierunt propter iniquitatem suam. Velut somnium surgentium, Domine, in civitate tua, imaginem ipsorum ad nihilum rediges. Unde in libro Sapientiæ vitiosi fatentur: Quid nobis profuit superbia? aut quid divitiarum jactantia contulit nobis? Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra, et tanquam nuntius præcurrens. Oculus qui eum viderat in temporali prosperitate et pompa, non videbit eum amplius in hac vita, quia post mortem non reditur ad statum sæculi hujus; neque ultra intuebitur eum locus ejus, id est, in pristino loco non conspicietur. Locus autem dicitur intueri materialiter, in quantum præbet id quod continet ad videndum, sicut inanimata dicuntur Creatorem suum laudare. Hinc ait Propheta: Quoniam spiritus pertransibit in illo, et non subsistet; et non cognoscet amplius locum suum.
paras.en: [[20:8|As a dream that fleeth away|Velut somnium avolans]], that is, quickly departing from the mind through forgetfulness, [[20:8|he shall not be found|non invenietur]] in his former life and glory; [[20:8|he shall pass as a vision of the night|transiet sicut visio nocturna]], which is wont to last but a moment: so shall he be taken out of life and perish utterly, as though he had never been here. So it is sung in the Psalms also: [[Ps 72:18|when they were lifted up thou hast cast them down|Dejecisti eos dum allevarentur]]. [[Ps 72:19|How are they brought to desolation? they have suddenly ceased to be: they have perished by reason of their iniquity.|Quomodo facti sunt in desolationem? Subito defecerunt, perierunt propter iniquitatem suam]] [[Ps 72:20|As the dream of them that awake, O Lord; so in thy city thou shalt bring their image to nothing.|Velut somnium surgentium, Domine, in civitate tua, imaginem ipsorum ad nihilum rediges]] Hence in the book of Wisdom the wicked confess: [[Wis 5:8|What hath pride profited us? or what advantage hath the boasting of riches brought us?|Quid nobis profuit superbia? aut quid divitiarum jactantia contulit nobis?]] [[Wis 5:9|All those things are passed away like a shadow, and like a post that runneth on|Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra, et tanquam nuntius præcurrens]]. [[20:9|The eyes that had seen him|Oculus qui eum viderat]] in temporal prosperity and pomp [[20:9|shall see him no more|non videbit eum amplius]] in this life, because after death there is no return to the state of this world; [[20:9|neither shall his place any more behold him|neque ultra intuebitur eum locus ejus]], that is, he shall not be seen in his former place. Now a place is said to behold in a material sense, inasmuch as it offers what it contains to be seen, as inanimate things are said to praise their Creator[[Ps 148:3||]] [the margin gives Ps. cxlviii, 3, 4, 7–9]. Hence the Prophet says: [[Ps 102:16|For the spirit shall pass in him, and he shall not be: and he shall know his place no more.|Quoniam spiritus pertransibit in illo, et non subsistet; et non cognoscet amplius locum suum]]

paras.t: Filii ejus atterentur egestate, id est, opibus sui patris privabuntur, et inopia affligentur. Quod non semper corporaliter agitur: ideo spiritualiter verius adimpletur, quod hi qui ejus sectantur hypocrisim, ex spiritualis refectionis carentia mente arescunt, et veris virtutum privantur divitiis. De qua inopia ait Psalmista: Divites eguerunt et esurierunt. Et manus, id est operationes, illius reddent illi dolorem suum, id est pœnam quam meruit, quoniam propter opera sua iniqua damnatur: juxta quod in Isaia scriptum est: Væ impio in malum; retributio enim manuum ejus fiet ei.
paras.en: [[20:10|His children shall be oppressed with want|Filii ejus atterentur egestate]], that is, they shall be deprived of their father's wealth and afflicted with poverty. Since this does not always happen bodily, it is more truly fulfilled spiritually: those who follow his hypocrisy wither in mind for lack of spiritual nourishment, and are deprived of the true riches of the virtues. Of this want the Psalmist says: [[Ps 33:11|The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger|Divites eguerunt et esurierunt]]. [[20:10|And his hands|Et manus]], that is, his works, [[20:10|shall render to him his sorrow|illius reddent illi dolorem suum]], that is, the punishment he has deserved, since he is damned for his wicked works: according to what is written in Isaias: [[Is 3:11|Woe to the wicked unto evil: for the reward of his hands shall be given him.|Væ impio in malum; retributio enim manuum ejus fiet ei]]

paras.t: Ossa ejus implebuntur vitiis adolescentiæ ejus, id est, etiam quum senuerit, propter peccata in adolescentia habita, in carne et ossibus affligetur. In quo videtur pungere sanctum Job, quod propter peccata diu præterita taliter puniatur usque ad intima. Vel sic: Ossa ejus, id est interiora et animæ fortiores potentiæ, implebuntur vitiis adolescentiæ ejus: quia perseverabit in solitis culpis, quemadmodum in Proverbiis habetur: Adolescens juxta viam suam, etiam quum senuerit, non recedet ab ea. Unde Daniel dicit tali: Inveterate dierum malorum, nunc advenerunt peccata tua. In Ezechiele quoque de impiis legitur: Iniquitates eorum in ossibus eorum. Quidam, per ossa hypocritæ, intelligunt ministros ac roboratores ejus in malo: qui vitiis ejus implentur ea sequendo, secundum quod Ecclesiasticus ait: Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus.
paras.en: [[20:11|His bones shall be filled with the vices of his youth|Ossa ejus implebuntur vitiis adolescentiæ ejus]], that is, even when he is old, he shall be afflicted in flesh and bones for the sins committed in his youth. In this he seems to sting holy Job, as being punished so, to the very marrow, for sins long past. Or thus: [[20:11|His bones|Ossa ejus]], that is, the inward and stronger powers of the soul, [[20:11|shall be filled with the vices of his youth|implebuntur vitiis adolescentiæ ejus]]: because he will persevere in his accustomed faults, as is found in Proverbs: [[Prov 22:6|A young man according to his way, even when he is old, he will not depart from it|Adolescens juxta viam suam, etiam quum senuerit, non recedet ab ea]]. Hence Daniel says to such a one: [[Dan 13:52|O thou that art grown old in evil days, now are thy sins come out|Inveterate dierum malorum, nunc advenerunt peccata tua]]. In Ezechiel also we read of the wicked: [[Ezech 32:27|their iniquities were in their bones|Iniquitates eorum in ossibus eorum]]. Some understand by the bones of the hypocrite his ministers and abettors in evil, who are filled with his vices by following them, according to what Ecclesiasticus says: [[Ecclus 10:2|As the judge of the people is himself, so also are his ministers|Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus]].

paras.t: Et cum eo in pulvere dormient, id est, in terra quiescent, deinde post resurrectionem communem in inferno pariter punientur. Cujus causam adjicit: Quum enim dulce fuerit in ore ejus malum, id est, iniquitas sua ei suavis ac placita fuerit, et de ea delectabiliter loqui inceperit: quales sunt illi præsertim, qui peccant ex habitu vitioso, seu deliberatione et certa malitia, non ex ignorantia, infirmitate, solave passione. De quibus in Proverbiis asseritur: Lætantur quum malefecerint, et exsultant in rebus pessimis; atque in Psalmo: Prodiit quasi ex adipe iniquitas eorum. Quum enim habitus sit velut altera natura, secundum philosophos, sicut delectabile est operari secundum naturalem inclinationem, ita delectat operantem operari secundum habitum quo impletur. Ideo in Proverbiis dictum est: Gaudium justo facere justitiam. Et alibi legitur: Stultitia gaudium stulto. Abscondet illud sub lingua sua, id est, impietatem suam occultat, excusat et palliat. Quocontra orat vir sanctus: Non declines cor meum in verba malitiæ, ad excusandas excusationes in peccatis. Et in Proverbiis ait Scriptura: Qui abscondit scelera sua, non dirigetur. Vel, Abscondit illud sub lingua sua, id est, in vitio perseverat: quemadmodum comedens dulce quid, tenet illud sub lingua, ut diutius delectetur ejus sapore.
paras.en: [[20:11|and they shall sleep with him in the dust|Et cum eo in pulvere dormient]], that is, they shall rest in the earth, and then, after the general resurrection, be punished together in hell. He adds the cause of this: [[20:12|For when evil shall be sweet in his mouth|Quum enim dulce fuerit in ore ejus malum]], that is, when his iniquity has been sweet and pleasing to him, and he has begun to speak of it with delight: such above all are those who sin from vicious habit, or with deliberation and set malice, not from ignorance, weakness, or passion alone. Of these it is affirmed in Proverbs: [[Prov 2:14|Who are glad when they have done evil, and rejoice in the most wicked things|Lætantur quum malefecerint, et exsultant in rebus pessimis]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 72:7|Their iniquity hath come forth, as it were from fatness|Prodiit quasi ex adipe iniquitas eorum]]. For since habit is as it were a second nature, according to the philosophers, then just as it is delightful to act according to natural inclination, so it delights the doer to act according to the habit with which he is filled. Therefore it is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 21:15|It is joy to the just to do judgment|Gaudium justo facere justitiam]] [Denis reads *justitiam*, justice, for the Vulgate's *judicium*]. And elsewhere we read: [[Prov 15:21|Folly is joy to the fool|Stultitia gaudium stulto]]. [[20:12|he will hide it under his tongue|Abscondet illud sub lingua sua]], that is, he hides his wickedness, excuses it and cloaks it. Against this the holy man prays: [[Ps 140:4|Incline not my heart to evil words; to make excuses in sins|Non declines cor meum in verba malitiæ, ad excusandas excusationes in peccatis]]. And in Proverbs the Scripture says: [[Prov 28:13|He that hideth his sins, shall not prosper|Qui abscondit scelera sua, non dirigetur]]. Or, [[20:12|he will hide it under his tongue|Abscondit illud sub lingua sua]], that is, he perseveres in vice: as one eating something sweet holds it under his tongue, so as to enjoy its taste the longer.

paras.t: Parcet illi, id est, peccatum suum pœnitendo non corrigit, neque ulciscitur; et non relinquet illud, cessando a culpa; et celabit in gutture suo, id est, aperte non confitebitur. Quocontra scriptum est: Fili mi, da gloriam Domino Deo, et confitere atque indica quid feceris; ne abscondas. Et Jacobus ait: Confitemini alterutrum peccata vestra. Itaque, tempore sanitatis, amore justitiæ et odio culpæ confiteamur, juxta illud Ecclesiastici: Ante mortem confitere; a mortuo quasi nihil perit confessio. Confiteberis vivens et sanus. Denique in his Sophar tangit beatum Job, quod ita deliciosum fuerit sibi peccare, quod nolit sua vitia confiteri, sed ea excuset ac neget, seque justificet. Verum istud est mollium, nil triste et durum in pœnitentia pati volentium.
paras.en: [[20:13|He will spare it|Parcet illi]], that is, he does not correct his sin by doing penance, nor avenge it; [[20:13|and not leave it|et non relinquet illud]] by ceasing from the fault; [[20:13|and will hide it in his throat|et celabit in gutture suo]], that is, he will not confess openly. Against this it is written: [[Jos 7:19|My son, give glory to the Lord God|Fili mi, da gloriam Domino Deo]], [[Jos 7:19|and confess|et confitere]], and declare [[Jos 7:19|what thou hast done, hide it not|quid feceris; ne abscondas]]. And James says: [[Jas 5:16|Confess therefore your sins one to another|Confitemini alterutrum peccata vestra]]. Let us therefore confess in the time of health, out of love of justice and hatred of sin, according to that of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 17:26|give glory before death|Ante mortem confitere]]; [[Ecclus 17:26|Praise perisheth from the dead as nothing|a mortuo quasi nihil perit confessio]]. [[Ecclus 17:27|whilst thou art alive and in health thou shalt give thanks|Confiteberis vivens et sanus]] [*confitere* and *confessio* mean both confessing and giving praise; Denis takes them of confession]. Lastly, in these words Sophar touches blessed Job, as though sinning had been so delightful to him that he would not confess his vices, but excused and denied them, and justified himself. But this belongs to the soft, who will suffer nothing sad or hard in penance.

paras.t: Panis ejus in utero illius, vertetur in fel aspidum intrinsecus: id est, refectio, qua se laute et de illicitis maleve acquisitis pavit, erit ei causa amarissimæ pœnæ ac damnationis: vel in humores venenosos atque mortiferos, justo Dei judicio, cibus suus sibi in suo utero convertetur, juxta illud Proverbiorum: Suavis est homini panis mendacii, et postea implebitur os ejus calculo. Divitias quas devoravit, id est, injuste rapuit et consumpsit, evomet, id est, turpiter perdet, vel intempestive ac dolorose amittet; et de ventre illius extrahet eas Deus, id est, districte ab eo requiret, torquendoque exiget quidquid impie habuit, egit, expendit.
paras.en: [[20:14|His bread in his belly shall be turned into the gall of asps within him|Panis ejus in utero illius, vertetur in fel aspidum intrinsecus]]: that is, the food with which he fed himself sumptuously, on things unlawful or ill gotten, shall be to him a cause of most bitter punishment and damnation; or, by the just judgment of God, his food shall be turned within his belly into poisonous and deadly humours, according to that of Proverbs: [[Prov 20:17|The bread of lying is sweet to a man: but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel|Suavis est homini panis mendacii, et postea implebitur os ejus calculo]]. [[20:15|The riches which he hath swallowed|Divitias quas devoravit]], that is, which he unjustly seized and consumed, [[20:15|he shall vomit up|evomet]], that is, he shall lose them shamefully, or part with them untimely and painfully; [[20:15|and God shall draw them out of his belly|et de ventre illius extrahet eas Deus]], that is, he will strictly require them of him, and by torment exact whatever he wickedly had, did and spent.

paras.t: Caput aspidum surget, id est, impium atque hypocritam invadet ut mordeat, intelligendo per caput aspidum, principem sævum sive diabolum. Sic S. Thomas exponit. Quæ expositio cuidam inepta videtur, asserenti quod in Hebræo ac libris correctis habeatur, Suget. Verumtamen B. Gregorius, diligentissimus libri hujus inspector, secundum utramque translationem, videlicet Septuaginta interpretum atque Hieronymi, legit et exponit, Surget, non, Suget. Hinc verius reor sic in Hebræo haberi, sicut Hieronymus transtulit, qui ubique asserit se Hebraicam veritatem secutum, nec quidquam de ea mutasse. Insuper arbitror quod verbum Hebraicum sit forte æquivocum ad Suget, et Surget. Attamen aliqui libri continent, Suget. Nam et Albertus ita exponit, dicendo: Aspis, serpens est incantatorem non audiens, pernecabile habens venenum, id est valde infectivum (quia mordendo interficit, juxta Thomam), designatque dæmones præsidentes obstinatis, doctores et prædicatores non audientibus: cujus aspidis caput sugit, qui cum delectatione suggestiones ejus acceptat. Quod sub aliqua metaphora Isaias sic dicit: Ova aspidum ruperunt, et telas araneæ texuerunt. Qui comederit de ovis eorum, morietur; et quod confotum est, erumpet in regulum. Itaque expositio Thomæ conveniens est. Et occidet eum lingua viperæ. Vipera genus serpentis est, lingua sua diffundentis venena: per quam detractor seu accusator vel dæmon impietatis persuasor exprimitur. A quo detractore, accusatore seu dæmone, hypocrita et iniquus corporaliter spiritualiterve necatur. Non videat per experimentum, id est non sortiatur, rivulos fluminis, torrentes, id est abundantiam temporalis prosperitatis aut opulentiæ accurrentis ut flumen, vel adhærentis et stantis ut torrens, mellis et butyri, id est, abundantiam dulcium ac delectabilium rerum non habeat.
paras.en: [[20:16|The head of asps|Caput aspidum]] shall rise [Denis reads *surget*, “shall rise”, with St Thomas; the Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims have *suget*, “shall suck”], that is, shall attack the wicked man and hypocrite so as to bite him, understanding by the head of asps the cruel prince, that is, the devil. So St Thomas explains it. This explanation seems unfitting to a certain writer, who asserts that in the Hebrew and in corrected books it reads *Suget* [shall suck]. Yet blessed Gregory, a most careful student of this book, reads and explains *Surget*, not *Suget*, according to both translations, that is, that of the Seventy translators and that of Jerome. Hence I think it truer that the Hebrew has it as Jerome translated it, who everywhere asserts that he followed the Hebrew truth and changed nothing of it. Moreover I think that the Hebrew word may perhaps be ambiguous between *Suget* and *Surget*. Still, some books have *Suget*. For Albert too explains it so, saying: The asp is a serpent that does not hear the charmer, having a most deadly poison, that is, very infectious (for it kills by biting, according to Thomas), and it signifies the demons who preside over the obstinate, who do not hear doctors and preachers: he sucks the head of this asp who accepts its suggestions with delight. This Isaias says under a certain metaphor thus: [[Is 59:5|They have broken the eggs of asps, and have woven the webs of spiders: he that shall eat of their eggs, shall die: and that which is brought out, shall be hatched into a basilisk|Ova aspidum ruperunt, et telas araneæ texuerunt. Qui comederit de ovis eorum, morietur; et quod confotum est, erumpet in regulum]]. And so the explanation of Thomas is fitting. [[20:16|and the viper's tongue shall kill him|Et occidet eum lingua viperæ]]. The viper is a kind of serpent that pours out poison with its tongue; by it is expressed the detractor or accuser, or the demon who persuades to wickedness. By this detractor, accuser or demon the hypocrite and wicked man is slain, bodily or spiritually. [[20:17|Let him not see|Non videat]] by experience, that is, let him not obtain, [[20:17|the streams of the river|rivulos fluminis]], [[20:17|the brooks|torrentes]], that is, an abundance of temporal prosperity or wealth, flowing in like a river, or clinging and standing like a brook, [[20:17|of honey and of butter|mellis et butyri]], that is, let him not have an abundance of sweet and delightful things.

paras.t: Luet quæ fecit omnia, id est, pro universis et singulis suis vitiis punietur: quemadmodum in Ezechiele Dominus ait: Unumquemque juxta vias suas judicabo. Deus enim nullum malum deserit impunitum, sicut nec aliquid in toto inordinatum relinquit: quod enim inordinatum est per culpam, ordinat ipse per pœnam. Nec tamen consumetur, id est, esse non desinet. Anima enim permanet immortalis; corpora quoque damnatorum resuscitata, non consumentur ab igne inferni. Mors quippe illius miseriæ, quæ in Apocalypsi dicitur mors secunda, non tollit esse et vitam naturæ, nec destruit corpora, sed æternaliter inest ac punit: nec ibi verificatur illud Philosophi, Nullum violentum perpetuum; sed (quod in Apocalypsi legitur) cruciabitur iniquus igne et sulfure, et fumus tormentorum ejus ascendet in sæcula sæculorum. Juxta multitudinem adinventionum suarum, id est excogitatarum malitiarum recentiumque culparum, sic et sustinebit tormenta inferni: quia pœna correspondet culpæ. Quo enim gravius et multiplicius quis peccavit, eo pœnalius affligetur, secundum illud Apocalypsis: Quantum glorificavit se et in deliciis fuit, tantum date illi tormentum et luctum. Et Sapiens: Fortioribus fortior instat cruciatus.
paras.en: [[20:18|He shall be punished for all that he did|Luet quæ fecit omnia]], that is, he shall be punished for each and every one of his vices, as the Lord says in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 18:30|will I judge every man according to his ways|Unumquemque juxta vias suas judicabo]]. For God leaves no evil unpunished, just as he leaves nothing at all out of order: what is put out of order by sin, he himself sets in order by punishment. [[20:18|and yet shall not be consumed|Nec tamen consumetur]], that is, he shall not cease to be. For the soul remains immortal, and the bodies of the damned also, once raised, shall not be consumed by the fire of hell. For the death of that misery, which in the Apocalypse is called [[Apoc 20:14|the second death|mors secunda]][[Apoc 21:8||]], does not take away being and the life of nature, nor destroy bodies, but abides in them eternally and punishes them: nor is that saying of the Philosopher verified there, Nothing violent is perpetual [the margin notes here: Error of Aristotle]; but (as we read in the Apocalypse) the wicked man [[Apoc 14:10|shall be tormented with fire and brimstone|cruciabitur iniquus igne et sulfure]], [[Apoc 14:11|And the smoke of their torments, shall ascend up for ever and ever|et fumus tormentorum ejus ascendet in sæcula sæculorum]]. [[20:18|according to the multitude of his devices|Juxta multitudinem adinventionum suarum]], that is, of the wickednesses he has thought out and of his fresh faults, [[20:18|so also shall he suffer|sic et sustinebit]] the torments of hell: for the punishment answers to the fault. For the more grievously and the more manifoldly anyone has sinned, the more painfully shall he be afflicted, according to that of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 18:7|As much as she hath glorified herself and lived in delicacies, so much torment and sorrow give ye to her|Quantum glorificavit se et in deliciis fuit, tantum date illi tormentum et luctum]]. And the Wise Man: [[Wis 6:9|a greater punishment is ready for the more mighty|Fortioribus fortior instat cruciatus]].

paras.t: Quoniam confringens, id est, violenter frangens, nudavit pauperis domum, inopem spoliando; rapuit quæ in pauperis domo invenit, et non ædificavit eam, id est, ablata non restituit, nec destructa reparavit. Talibus Dominus loquitur per Isaiam: Rapina pauperis in domo vestra est. Quare atteritis populum meum, et facies pauperum commolitis? Nec est satiatus venter ejus, id est pauperis, quoniam rebus suis sibi ablatis, sufficientiam non habebat. Vel, Non est satiatus venter ejus, id est, cor præfati iniqui opibus non est impletum, sed plura appetiit: juxta illud Proverbiorum, Venter impiorum insatiabilis. Et Ecclesiastes ait: Avarus non impletur pecunia. Et, quum habuerit quæ concupierat, possidere non poterit ea diu: quia vel morte prævenietur, sicut diviti cuidam dicitur: Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetent a te; quæ autem parasti, cujus erunt? Vel illa ab eo tollentur, ut Salomon ait: Qui amat divitias, fructum non capiet ex eis. Rursusque: Divitiæ congregatæ in malum domini sui, pereunt in afflictione pessima.
paras.en: [[20:19|Because he broke in|Quoniam confringens]], that is, breaking violently, he [[20:19|stripped|nudavit]] the poor man's house [Denis reads *pauperis domum*, “the poor man's house”, where the Vulgate has *pauperes: domum*, “the poor: a house”], despoiling the needy; [[20:19|he hath violently taken away|rapuit]] what he found in the poor man's house, [[20:19|which he did not build|et non ædificavit eam]], that is, he did not restore what he took away, nor repair what he destroyed. To such the Lord speaks by Isaias: [[Is 3:14|the spoil of the poor is in your house|Rapina pauperis in domo vestra est]]. [[Is 3:15|Why do you consume my people, and grind the faces of the poor?|Quare atteritis populum meum, et facies pauperum commolitis?]] [[20:20|And yet his belly was not filled|Nec est satiatus venter ejus]], that is, the poor man's, since, his goods having been taken from him, he did not have enough. Or, [[20:20|his belly was not filled|Non est satiatus venter ejus]], that is, the heart of the wicked man spoken of was not filled with wealth, but desired more: according to that of Proverbs, [[Prov 13:25|the belly of the wicked is never to be filled|Venter impiorum insatiabilis]]. And Ecclesiastes says: [[Eccles 5:9|A covetous man shall not be satisfied with money|Avarus non impletur pecunia]]. [[20:20|and when he hath the things he coveted|Et, quum habuerit quæ concupierat]], [[20:20|he shall not be able to possess|possidere non poterit]] them for long: either because he will be overtaken by death, as is said to a certain rich man: [[Luke 12:20|Thou fool, this night do they require thy soul of thee. And whose shall those things be which thou hast provided?|Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetent a te; quæ autem parasti, cujus erunt?]] Or else they shall be taken from him, as Solomon says: [[Eccles 5:9|he that loveth riches shall reap no fruit from them|Qui amat divitias, fructum non capiet ex eis]]. And again: [[Eccles 5:12|riches kept to the hurt of the owner|Divitiæ congregatæ in malum domini sui]], [[Eccles 5:13|For they are lost with very great affliction|pereunt in afflictione pessima]].

paras.t: Non remansit de cibo ejus, id est, totum in suum usum convertit, nihil pauperibus tribuit, prout in Ezechiele fertur: Hæc fuit iniquitas Sodomæ, superbia, saturitas panis, abundantia, otium, et quia manum egeno et pauperi non porrigebat. Cujus congrua pœna subjungitur: propterea nihil remanebit de bonis ejus, id est, omnia sua ei tollentur, saltem in morte, juxta id Psalmi: Dormierunt somnum suum, et nihil invenerunt omnes viri divitiarum in manibus suis. Quum satiatus fuerit, id est ditatus, arctabitur sollicitudine. Denique satiatus, nimia ventris repletione arctatur intra uteri sui pellem, quæ ultra extendi non valet: sicque torsiones et dolores patitur ventris. Æstuabit anxietate perdendi quæ habet. Divitiæ enim cum timore possidentur. Et omnis dolor, id est perfecta seu multiplex pœna, irruet super eum, partim in sæculo isto, deinde in futuro. Ex immoderantia etenim potus et cibi, varii dolores oriuntur in corpore. Hinc scriptum est in Ecclesiastico: Quam sufficiens homini erudito vinum exiguum! et in dormiendo non laborabis ab illo, et non senties dolorem. Vigilia, et cholera, et tortura homini infrunito, id est intemperato.
paras.en: [[20:21|There was nothing left of his meat|Non remansit de cibo ejus]], that is, he turned it all to his own use and gave nothing to the poor, as is said in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 16:49|this was the iniquity of Sodom thy sister, pride, fulness of bread, and abundance|Hæc fuit iniquitas Sodomæ, superbia, saturitas panis, abundantia]], [[Ezech 16:49|idleness|otium]], and that [[Ezech 16:49|they did not put forth their hand to the needy, and the poor|manum egeno et pauperi non porrigebat]]. Its fitting punishment is added: [[20:21|and therefore nothing shall continue of his goods|propterea nihil remanebit de bonis ejus]], that is, all he has shall be taken from him, at least in death, according to that of the Psalm: [[Ps 75:6|They have slept their sleep; and all the men of riches have found nothing in their hands|Dormierunt somnum suum, et nihil invenerunt omnes viri divitiarum in manibus suis]]. [[20:22|When he shall be filled|Quum satiatus fuerit]], that is, enriched, [[20:22|he shall be straitened|arctabitur]] by care. Or again: when filled, he is straitened by too great a filling of the belly within the skin of his womb, which can stretch no further, and so he suffers gripings and pains of the belly. [[20:22|he shall burn|Æstuabit]] with anxiety at losing what he has, for riches are possessed with fear. [[20:22|and every sorrow|Et omnis dolor]], that is, a complete or manifold punishment, [[20:22|shall fall upon him|irruet super eum]], partly in this world, then in the next. For from immoderate drink and food various pains arise in the body. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 31:22|How sufficient is a little wine for a man well taught, and in sleeping thou shalt not be uneasy with it, and thou shalt feel no pain.|Quam sufficiens homini erudito vinum exiguum! et in dormiendo non laborabis ab illo, et non senties dolorem]] [[Ecclus 31:23|Watching, and choler, and gripes, are with an intemperate man|Vigilia, et cholera, et tortura homini infrunito]], that is, one without temperance [Denis glosses the rare *infrunitus*, which the Douay-Rheims already renders “intemperate”].

paras.t: Deinde Sophar quasi zelo justitiæ addit: Utinam impleatur venter ejus, ut emittat in eum iram furoris sui, id est, ad hoc temporaliter sic abundet, ut Deus districto eum condemnet judicio: sicut de impiis ait per Sophoniam, Effundam super eos indignationem meam et omnem iram furoris mei; et pluat super illum bellum suum, id est, desuper copiose ingerat ei pœnam totaliter exterminantem ac superantem, non paternaliter castigantem: secundum illud in Psalmo, Pluit super peccatores laqueos.
paras.en: Then Sophar, as if from zeal for justice, adds: [[20:23|May his belly be filled, that God may send forth the wrath of his indignation upon him|Utinam impleatur venter ejus, ut emittat in eum iram furoris sui]], that is, may he so abound in temporal things to this end, that God may condemn him with strict judgment: as he says of the wicked through Sophonias, determined [[Soph 3:8|to pour upon them my indignation, all my fierce anger|Effundam super eos indignationem meam et omnem iram furoris mei]]; [[20:23|and rain down his war upon him|et pluat super illum bellum suum]], that is, may he heap upon him plenteously from above a punishment that wholly destroys and overwhelms, not one that chastises as a father does: according to that in the Psalm, [[Ps 10:7|He shall rain snares upon sinners|Pluit super peccatores laqueos]].

paras.t: Fugiet arma ferrea, et irruet in arcum æreum, id est, minora vitabit adversa, videlicet flagella, labores et pœnas vitæ præsentis, incidetque supplicium infernale, quod omnium adversorum est maximum: quia enim in sæculo isto non vult pro peccatis suis dolere, satisfacere et puniri, meretur æternaliter cruciari. Itaque juxta Albertum, per ferrum, quod cetera domat metalla, ut dicitur in Daniele, exprimitur præsens pœna, qua Deus quasi armatur ad domandos corrigendosque impios, prout in Sapientiæ libro fertur: Accipiet armaturam zelus illius, et armabit creaturam ad ultionem inimicorum. Hanc pœnam injusti, pœnitentiam vitantes, refugiunt, dicente Psalmista: In labore hominum non sunt, et cum hominibus non flagellabuntur. Porro arcum nominat æreum, prout æs dicit commixtionem cupri vel stanni cum plumbo: quia æs, quia imputribile est, æternam pœnam significat. Dicitque arcum, quoniam profunde ac de longe ferit. Qui arcus æreus eductus manu sagittantis, et egrediens de vagina sua, id est corio quo sagittarii ferunt arcum, et fulgurans in amaritudine sua, id est pœna quam imprimit. Per arcum istum, ut patuit, intelligitur infernalis cruciatus, cujus velut vagina est occultum Dei judicium, seu præscientia ejus, qui tempore præstituto pœnam hanc in aperto infligit cum fulguratione, id est terrore, impetu et splendore justitiæ, sicut fulgur ruit de cœlo repente ac violenter et clare.
paras.en: [[20:24|He shall flee from weapons of iron, and shall fall upon a bow of brass|Fugiet arma ferrea, et irruet in arcum æreum]], that is, he shall escape the lesser adversities, namely the scourges, labours and punishments of the present life, and shall fall into the punishment of hell, which is the greatest of all adversities: for because in this world he will not grieve for his sins, make satisfaction and be punished, he deserves to be tormented eternally. And so, according to Albert, by iron, which subdues the other metals, as is said in Daniel[[Dan 2:40||]], is expressed present punishment, with which God, as it were, arms himself to subdue and correct the wicked, as is said in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:18|And his zeal will take armour, and he will arm the creature for the revenge of his enemies|Accipiet armaturam zelus illius, et armabit creaturam ad ultionem inimicorum]]. This punishment the unjust, shunning penance, flee from, as the Psalmist says: [[Ps 72:5|They are not in the labour of men: neither shall they be scourged like other men|In labore hominum non sunt, et cum hominibus non flagellabuntur]]. Further, he names the bow brazen, in that brass means an alloy of copper or tin with lead: because brass, since it does not decay, signifies eternal punishment. And he says a bow, because it strikes deep and from afar. This brazen bow [[20:25|is drawn out|eductus]] by the archer's hand, [[20:25|and cometh forth from its scabbard|et egrediens de vagina sua]], that is, from the leather case in which archers carry the bow, [[20:25|and glittereth in his bitterness|et fulgurans in amaritudine sua]], that is, in the pain it inflicts [the Douay-Rheims supplies “the sword”; Denis takes the verse of the bow of v. 24]. By this bow, as has been shown, is understood the torment of hell, whose scabbard, as it were, is the hidden judgment of God, or his foreknowledge, who at the appointed time inflicts this punishment openly with lightning, that is, with the terror, onset and splendour of justice, as lightning rushes from heaven suddenly, violently and brightly.

paras.t: Vadent et venient super eum horribiles, id est, dæmones eum ad libitum conculcabunt, et liberam super eum potestatem habebunt, ad puniendum secundum quod meruit. Omnes tenebræ absconditæ sunt in occultis ejus: id est, interiores et exteriores tenebræ inveniuntur in secretis inferni latibulis, quo ipse deveniet; in secretisque conscientiæ suæ seu intellectus ac voluntatis, latent omnium tenebræ vitiorum. Hinc dicitur: Projicite eum in tenebras exteriores. De interioribus quoque tenebris ait Psalmista: Nescierunt, neque intellexerunt: in tenebris ambulant. Unde superius de inferno inductum est: Antequam vadam ad terram tenebrosam et opertam mortis caligine.
paras.en: [[20:25|the terrible ones shall go and come upon him|Vadent et venient super eum horribiles]], that is, the demons shall trample him at their pleasure, and shall have free power over him, to punish him as he has deserved. [[20:26|All darkness is hid in his secret places|Omnes tenebræ absconditæ sunt in occultis ejus]]: that is, inner and outer darkness is found in the secret hiding places of hell, whither he shall come; and in the secret places of his conscience, that is, of his understanding and will, lies hid the darkness of all vices. Hence it is said: Cast him [[Matt 22:13|into the exterior darkness|in tenebras exteriores]] [the margin here is illegible; Denis's wording is closest to Matt 22:13, cf. Matt 25:30]. Of the inner darkness too the Psalmist says: [[Ps 81:5|They have not known nor understood: they walk on in darkness|Nescierunt, neque intellexerunt: in tenebris ambulant]]. Hence it was said above of hell: [[Job 10:21|Before I go and return no more, to a land that is dark and covered with the mist of death|Antequam vadam ad terram tenebrosam et opertam mortis caligine]].

paras.t: Devorabit eum ignis qui non succenditur, scilicet ignis infernalis, qui ab homine non nutritur nova materia, neque succenditur: sed semel a Deo succensus, manet in perpetuo in suo vigore, juxta illud Isaiæ: Præparata est ab heri Topheth, id est gehenna, a rege præparata, profunda et dilatata. Flatus Domini sicut torrens sulfuris succendens eam. Dicitur autem ignis inferni damnatos devorare, non auferendo ab eis esse et vivere, sed omne bene esse, et absorbendo seu totaliter occupando eos suo prædoloroso impetu et vigore. Hinc fertur in Psalmo: Pones eos ut clibanum ignis in tempore vultus tui; Dominus in ira sua conturbabit eos, et devorabit eos ignis. Itemque: Cadent super eos carbones, in ignem dejicies eos; in miseriis non subsistent. Hinc Christus se dicturum nuntiat: Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Affligetur relictus in tabernaculo suo, id est infernali ergastulo, unde nunquam eruetur seu redimetur. Insuper, post diem judicii punietur, relictus in tabernaculo, id est corpore proprio, sibi tunc uniendo, ut puniatur pariter in utroque, scilicet anima et corpore, sicut per utrumque et in utroque peccavit, et impie delectatus est.
paras.en: [[20:26|a fire that is not kindled shall devour him|Devorabit eum ignis qui non succenditur]], namely the fire of hell, which is not fed by man with new fuel nor kindled by him, but, once kindled by God, abides for ever in its strength, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 30:33|Topheth is prepared from yesterday|Præparata est ab heri Topheth]], that is, gehenna, [[Is 30:33|prepared by the king, deep, and wide|a rege præparata, profunda et dilatata]]. [[Is 30:33|the breath of the Lord as a torrent of brimstone kindling it|Flatus Domini sicut torrens sulfuris succendens eam]]. Now the fire of hell is said to devour the damned, not by taking from them being and life, but all well-being, and by swallowing them up, that is, wholly seizing upon them with its most painful onset and strength. Hence it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 20:10|Thou shalt make them as an oven of fire, in the time of thy anger: the Lord shall trouble them in his wrath, and fire shall devour them.|Pones eos ut clibanum ignis in tempore vultus tui; Dominus in ira sua conturbabit eos, et devorabit eos ignis]] And again: [[Ps 139:11|Burning coals shall fall upon them; thou wilt cast them down into the fire: in miseries they shall not be able to stand|Cadent super eos carbones, in ignem dejicies eos; in miseriis non subsistent]]. Hence Christ announces that he will say: Go, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]]. [[20:26|he shall be afflicted when left in his tabernacle|Affligetur relictus in tabernaculo suo]], that is, in the prison house of hell, from which he shall never be rescued or redeemed. Moreover, after the day of judgment he shall be punished, [[20:26|left in his tabernacle|relictus in tabernaculo]], that is, in his own body, which shall then be united to him again, so that he may be punished alike in both, namely in soul and body, as through both and in both he sinned and took wicked delight.

paras.t: Revelabunt cœli iniquitatem ejus, id est, cives cœlestes seu angeli sancti contra eum in die judicii testimonium proferent, et divina virtute peccata ejus omnibus innotescent; et terra adversus eum consurget, id est, homines virtuosi qui in terra mox ante judicium erunt, morientur, ac suscitabuntur, contra eum zelo justitiæ movebuntur. Vel, Terra, id est elementum terræ, adversus eum consurget, id est, divinæ ultionis instrumentum ac adjutorium erit in impio, ipsumque damnabilem demonstrabit, eo quod Creatorem suum offenderit. Unde sapiens quidam asserit: Pugnabit cum Deo orbis terrarum contra insensatos. Quod in eodem libro quasi exponitur, quum dicitur: Creatura enim tibi Creatori deserviens, excandescet in tormentum adversus injustos. Hinc fertur in Psalmo: Deus manifeste veniet. Ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet; et in circuitu ejus tempestas valida. Advocabit cœlum desursum, et terram discernere populum suum. Insuper, in die judicii terra consurget adversus injustum, quia unus iniquus ac reprobus alium tunc damnabit comparative: quia videlicet peccatum unius, comparatione alterius, gravius apparebit; damnatio quoque unius, comparatione alterius, justior ostendetur. Hinc Christus in Evangelio, Regina, inquit, Austri surget in judicio cum generatione ista, utpote Judæorum, et damnabit eam. Idemque ait de Ninivitis.
paras.en: [[20:27|The heavens shall reveal his iniquity|Revelabunt cœli iniquitatem ejus]], that is, the citizens of heaven, or the holy angels, shall bear witness against him on the day of judgment, and by the power of God his sins shall be made known to all; [[20:27|and the earth shall rise up against him|et terra adversus eum consurget]], that is, the virtuous men who shall be on the earth just before the judgment, and shall die and be raised up, shall be moved against him with zeal for justice. Or, [[20:27|the earth|Terra]], that is, the element of earth, [[20:27|shall rise up against him|adversus eum consurget]], that is, it shall be an instrument and helper of God's vengeance upon the wicked man, and shall show him to be worthy of damnation, because he offended his Creator. Hence a certain wise man asserts: [[Wis 5:21|the whole world shall fight with him against the unwise|Pugnabit cum Deo orbis terrarum contra insensatos]]. This is as it were explained in the same book, when it is said: [[Wis 16:24|For the creature serving thee, the Creator, is made fierce against the unjust for their punishment|Creatura enim tibi Creatori deserviens, excandescet in tormentum adversus injustos]]. Hence it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 49:3|God shall come manifestly|Deus manifeste veniet]]. [[Ps 49:3|A fire shall burn before him: and a mighty tempest shall be round about him|Ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet; et in circuitu ejus tempestas valida]]. [[Ps 49:4|He shall call heaven from above, and the earth, to judge his people|Advocabit cœlum desursum, et terram discernere populum suum]]. Moreover, on the day of judgment the earth shall rise up against the unjust man, because one wicked and reprobate man shall then condemn another by comparison: that is, the sin of one shall appear more grievous in comparison with another's, and the damnation of one shall be shown more just in comparison with another's. Hence Christ in the Gospel says: [[Matt 12:42|The queen|Regina]], he says, [[Matt 12:42|of the south shall rise in judgment with this generation|Austri surget in judicio cum generatione ista]], namely that of the Jews, [[Matt 12:42|and shall condemn it|et damnabit eam]][[Luke 11:31||]]. And he says the same of the Ninivites[[Matt 12:41||]][[Luke 11:32||]].

paras.t: Apertum erit germen domus illius: id est, operatio vitiosa, quæ nunc in domo conscientiæ suæ celatur, tunc erit omnibus manifesta; germen quoque domus suæ, id est proles et familia sua, ipsius sequens peccata, erit tunc aperta, quantum ad vitia in quibus interim latet. Hinc ait Apostolus: Veniet Dominus, et revelabit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestabit consilia cordium. Christus etiam protestatur: Non est occultum quod non reveletur. Unde, ut hanc confusionem non incurramus, Ecclesiasticus nobis dicit: Fili, non semines mala in sulcis injustitiæ, et non metes ea in septuplum. Detrahetur germen præfatum in die furoris Domini, id est in die metuendæ ultionis Dei ac sui judicii, in infernum. Opera enim illorum sequuntur illos. Juxta quem modum Petrus de apostatis angelis scribit: Deus angelis peccantibus non pepercit, sed rudentibus inferni detractos, in tartarum tradidit in judicium cruciandos reservari. Sic in Apocalypsi de reprobo scriptum est: Hic bibet de vino iræ furoris Dei omnipotentis.
paras.en: [[20:28|The offspring of his house shall be exposed|Apertum erit germen domus illius]]: that is, the vicious working which is now hidden in the house of his conscience shall then be manifest to all; the offspring of his house, too, that is, his children and household who follow his sins, shall then be exposed, as to the vices in which it lies hid meanwhile. Hence the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 4:5|until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts|Veniet Dominus, et revelabit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestabit consilia cordium]]. Christ also declares: [[Luke 8:17|there is not any thing secret that shall not be made manifest|Non est occultum quod non reveletur]]. Therefore, that we may not incur this shame, Ecclesiasticus says to us: [[Ecclus 7:3|My son, sow not evils in the furrows of injustice, and thou shalt not reap them sevenfold|Fili, non semines mala in sulcis injustitiæ, et non metes ea in septuplum]]. [[20:28|he shall be pulled down|Detrahetur]] (that is, the aforesaid offspring) [[20:28|in the day of God's wrath|in die furoris Domini]], that is, in the day of God's dreadful vengeance and of his judgment, into hell. [[Apoc 14:13|For their works follow them|Opera enim illorum sequuntur illos]]. In the same way Peter writes of the apostate angels: [[2 Pet 2:4|God spared not the angels that sinned, but delivered them, drawn down by infernal ropes to the lower hell, unto torments, to be reserved unto judgment|Deus angelis peccantibus non pepercit, sed rudentibus inferni detractos, in tartarum tradidit in judicium cruciandos reservari]]. So in the Apocalypse it is written of the reprobate: [[Apoc 14:10|He also shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God|Hic bibet de vino iræ furoris Dei omnipotentis]] [Denis's wording adds *furoris … omnipotentis*, “of the fury of almighty God”, as in Apoc 19:15].

paras.t: Postremo epilogans, subdit: Hæc damnatio est pars hominis impii a Deo, id est merces et res quam suis peccatis meruit sibi a Deo retribui; et hæreditas verborum ejus, id est infelix pœnæ æternæ possessio, quam ex excessu verborum suorum promeruit a Domino sibi infligi: quemadmodum in Apocalypsi de reprobis legitur: Pars illorum erit in stagno ardenti igne et sulfure: quod est mors secunda. Quum enim in hac vita prætulerit caduca, vana et fœtida superdignissimo Creatori, nec eum præ cunctis elegit atque dilexit, ut dicere posset, Dominus pars hæreditatis meæ; justissimum est, ut hanc infelicissimam partem pro præmio sortiatur, nec delectetur in Deo altissimo, sed torqueatur a rebus vilissimis in infimo loco.
paras.en: Lastly, summing up, he adds: [[20:29|This|Hæc]] damnation [[20:29|is the portion of a wicked man from God|est pars hominis impii a Deo]], that is, the wages and the thing he deserved by his sins to have paid back to him by God; [[20:29|and the inheritance of his doings|et hæreditas verborum ejus]] [*verborum*, literally “of his words”, which Denis takes in that sense], that is, the unhappy possession of eternal punishment, which for the excess of his words he has deserved to have inflicted on him [[20:29|from the Lord|a Domino]]: as we read in the Apocalypse of the reprobate: [[Apoc 21:8|they shall have their portion in the pool burning with fire and brimstone, which is the second death|Pars illorum erit in stagno ardenti igne et sulfure: quod est mors secunda]]. For since in this life he preferred perishable, vain and foul things to the most worthy Creator, and did not choose and love him above all, so as to be able to say, [[Ps 15:5|The Lord is the portion of my inheritance|Dominus pars hæreditatis meæ]], it is most just that he should receive this most unhappy portion for his reward, and not delight in the most high God, but be tormented by the vilest things in the lowest place.

paras.t: Omnia hæc Sophar de hypocrita ita induxit, ut per ea beatum Job notaret. Quem enim vidit a Deo percussum, non credidit bona quæ egit, corde simplici operatum. Præterea constat ex his, quam evidentissime Sophar posuit vitam post hanc vitam, et animam immortalem, divinum judicium et infernum. Similiter de aliis duobus amicis Job est sentiendum. Sed et Thomas hoc loco fatetur sic esse, dicens quod Sophar, audita sententia sancti Job de futura resurrectione, acquievit: idcirco dixit, Doctrinam qua me arguis, audiam. Sed hoc verisimile non videtur. Si enim acquievisset jam primo de animæ immortalitate, hoc fuisset, quod rationes Job eum compulissent ad consentiendum. Sed nondum per argumenta Job inductus fuit ad credendum quod homo in hoc sæculo affligatur a Deo, nisi pro suo peccato. Propter quod toto capitulo isto locutus est contra hypocritam, ad innuendum quod Job fuit hypocrita. Insuper, dato quod jam acquievisset beato Job de vita futura, non tamen (ut apparet) tot et tanta prosecutus esset de ea in isto capitulo: in quo multa quasi ex proprio sensu disseruit de retributione futura, judicioque divino, quæ ante in hac disputatione a sancto Job non audivit.
paras.en: All these things Sophar brought in about the hypocrite so as to brand blessed Job by them. For seeing him struck by God, he did not believe that the good he did was done with a simple heart. Further, it is clear from these words how very plainly Sophar held a life after this life, and an immortal soul, the judgment of God, and hell. The same is to be thought of Job's other two friends. And Thomas too admits at this place that it is so, saying that Sophar, having heard holy Job's opinion on the future resurrection, acquiesced: and therefore said, [[20:3|The doctrine with which thou reprovest me, I will hear|Doctrinam qua me arguis, audiam]]. But this does not seem likely. For if he had already acquiesced at the first about the immortality of the soul, this would have been because Job's reasons had compelled him to agree. But he had not yet been brought by Job's arguments to believe that a man is afflicted by God in this world otherwise than for his own sin. For this reason he spoke against the hypocrite through this whole chapter, to hint that Job was a hypocrite. Moreover, granted that he had already acquiesced to blessed Job about the life to come, yet (as it appears) he would not have pursued so many and such great things about it in this chapter, in which he discoursed much, as if from his own mind, on the retribution to come and on the judgment of God, which he had not heard before from holy Job in this disputation.

20.title: De intelligentia morali ejusdem capituli vicesimi.
20.title_en: On the moral understanding of the same twentieth chapter

paras.t: Circa exordium expositionis præsentis capituli, dicit B. Gregorius, quod amici Job perversi non erant. Ex quo elicitur quod peccatum eorum, quod contra Job disputando incurrerunt, non ex malitia prodiit, sed ex ignorantia magis et quodam errore circa providentiam Dei, ut sæpius tactum est. Imo, ex zelo Dei se motos putabant ad contradicendum beato Job, quia videbatur eis providentiæ derogare divinæ: et plane ex zelo quodam Dei incitabantur, sed ex zelo non ordinato, quem et Judæos habuisse incredulos testatur Apostolus, Testimonium, inquiens, perhibeo illis quia zelum Dei habent, sed non secundum scientiam, id est discretionem.
paras.en: At the beginning of the exposition of the present chapter blessed Gregory says that Job's friends were not perverse. From which it is drawn that their sin, which they incurred by disputing against Job, did not come from malice, but rather from ignorance and a certain error about the providence of God, as has often been touched on. Indeed, they thought themselves moved by zeal for God to contradict blessed Job, because he seemed to them to detract from divine providence: and they were plainly stirred by a certain zeal for God, but by a zeal not well ordered, such as the Apostle testifies the unbelieving Jews too had, saying: [[Rom 10:2|I bear them witness that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge|Testimonium, inquiens, perhibeo illis quia zelum Dei habent, sed non secundum scientiam]], that is, discretion.

paras.t: Itaque, quoniam in fine præcedentis capituli Job de resurrectione et judicio futuris in die novissimo apertissime prophetavit, Respondens Sophar, dicit: Idcirco cogitationes meæ variæ succedunt sibi: id est, quoniam credo me sicut et te resurrecturum, atque divinitus judicandum, ob id diversis considerationibus angor, et ex corde sollicitor propriam sciens fragilitatem, culpabilitatem et insufficientiam, divinæque mentis sanctitatem, perfectionem et æquitatem, ac judiciorum ejus præhorrendum rigorem, reproborum etiam calamitatem æternam. Et mens in diversa rapitur, considerando diversa, et præmeditando qualiter respondeat coram Deo, ne a dæmonibus convincatur, ne ab angelis confundatur, ne perdat æternalia cœlestis gaudia paradisi, ne deputetur sempiternis tormentis inferni. Sic ergo et nos in corde nostro describamus ac imaginemur ordinem, terrorem et modum extremi judicii: quomodo universi resurgent, et ad judicii locum convenient; quomodo terra tota tunc stabit in horribili conflagratione ignis permaximi. Desuper apparebit omnipotens, justus, infallibilis Judex, cum innumerabilibus angelorum Sanctorumque millibus: aderunt et crudelissimi dæmones adversantes. Deorsum patens chaos gehennæ; inæstimabilis numerus damnandæ, tristissimæ, reprobæ turbæ; quod erit damnationis æternæ præstolari sententiam. Si hæc omnia et cetera judicium illud concernentia perpendamus, experiemur quid sit quod Sophar fatetur, dicendo: Idcirco cogitationes meæ variæ succedunt sibi, et mens in diversa rapitur.
paras.en: So, since at the end of the preceding chapter Job prophesied most openly of the resurrection and the judgment to come at the last day[[Job 19:25||]], [[20:1|Sophar the Naamathite answered, and said|Respondens Sophar, dicit]]: [[20:2|Therefore various thoughts succeed one another in me|Idcirco cogitationes meæ variæ succedunt sibi]]: that is, since I believe that I shall rise, as thou too wilt, and be judged by God, on that account I am tormented by various considerations, and troubled at heart, knowing my own frailty, guilt and insufficiency, and the holiness, perfection and equity of the divine mind, and the dreadful rigour of his judgments, and the eternal calamity of the reprobate. [[20:2|and my mind is hurried away to different things|Et mens in diversa rapitur]], considering different things, and thinking beforehand how it shall answer before God, lest it be convicted by the demons, lest it be confounded by the angels, lest it lose the eternal joys of the heavenly paradise, lest it be assigned to the everlasting torments of hell. So let us too picture and imagine in our heart the order, the terror and the manner of the last judgment: how all will rise and come together to the place of judgment; how the whole earth will then stand in the horrible burning of a very great fire. Above will appear the almighty, just and infallible Judge, with innumerable thousands of angels and saints[[Luke 9:26||]][[Jude 1:14||]]: and the most cruel demons will be there as adversaries. Below, the chaos of hell lying open; the countless number of the sorrowful and reprobate crowd to be damned; what it will be to await the sentence of eternal damnation. If we weigh all these things and the others that concern that judgment, we shall find by experience what it is that Sophar confesses, saying: *Therefore various thoughts succeed one another in me, and my mind is hurried away to different things.*

paras.t: Doctrinam qua me arguis, audiam. Ita et nos verba informatoria seu increpatoria modeste et longanimiter audiamus, non impetuose interrumpamus tanquam brutales, pensantes illud Ecclesiastici: Esto mansuetus ad audiendum verbum Dei; illud quoque Proverbiorum: Qui prius respondet quam audiat, stultum se esse demonstrat, et confusione dignum.
paras.en: [[20:3|The doctrine with which thou reprovest me, I will hear|Doctrinam qua me arguis, audiam]]. So let us too hear words of instruction or rebuke modestly and patiently, and not break in on them violently like brutes, weighing that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 5:13|Be meek to hear the word|Esto mansuetus ad audiendum verbum Dei]] [Denis adds *of God*]; and that of Proverbs: [[Prov 18:13|He that answereth before he heareth, sheweth himself to be a fool, and worthy of confusion|Qui prius respondet quam audiat, stultum se esse demonstrat, et confusione dignum]].

paras.t: Et spiritus intelligentiæ meæ respondebit mihi. Potest hoc de Spiritu Sancto exponi, qui dicitur spiritus intelligentiæ nostræ, id est, spiritus a quo causatur et profluit omnis cognitio nostra. De quo loquitur Christus: Quum autem venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem. Unde et infra asseritur: Inspiratio Omnipotentis dat intelligentiam. Qui nobis respondet, id est, scientiam respondendi infundit, de dubiis quoque certificat; qui nunc per se ipsum, nunc per angelum sanctum, nunc per prælatum seu proximum, nunc per Scripturam nobis respondet, nos docet, dicente Apostolo: Dabit tibi Dominus de omnibus intellectum. Hinc scriptum est: Si quis vestrum indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo, et dabitur ei. Postulet autem in fide nil hæsitans. Itaque ad Spiritus Sancti illuminationem semper confugiamus, eum pro sapientia suppliciter exoremus, ejus directioni in omnibus jugiter atque humillime innitamur.
paras.en: [[20:3|and the spirit of my understanding shall answer for me|Et spiritus intelligentiæ meæ respondebit mihi]] [literally *shall answer me*]. This can be expounded of the Holy Spirit, who is called the spirit of our understanding, that is, the spirit from whom all our knowledge is caused and flows. Of him Christ says: [[John 16:13|But when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will teach you all truth|Quum autem venerit ille Spiritus veritatis, docebit vos omnem veritatem]]. Hence it is also asserted below: [[Job 32:8|the inspiration of the Almighty giveth understanding|Inspiratio Omnipotentis dat intelligentiam]]. He answers us, that is, pours in the knowledge of how to answer, and makes us certain about doubtful things; he answers and teaches us now by himself, now by a holy angel, now by a prelate or a neighbour, now by Scripture, as the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 2:7|the Lord will give thee in all things understanding|Dabit tibi Dominus de omnibus intellectum]]. Hence it is written: [[Jas 1:5|if any of you want wisdom, let him ask of God|Si quis vestrum indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo]], [[Jas 1:5|And it shall be given him|et dabitur ei]]. [[Jas 1:6|But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering|Postulet autem in fide nil hæsitans]]. So let us always take refuge in the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit, beseech him humbly for wisdom, and lean constantly and most humbly on his direction in all things.

paras.t: Laus impiorum brevis est. Nonne frequenter pravissimi usque ad finem vitæ suæ a multis laudantur? quemadmodum fertur in Psalmo: Quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ, et iniquus benedicitur. Itemque in Proverbiis: Qui derelinquunt legem, laudant impium. Denique, nonne usque in præsens Jupiter, Neptunus, Venus, Diana, ac ceteri dii ac deæ gentilium, olim homines vitiosi, laudantur a suis cultoribus Tartaris sive similibus, sicut et Mahometus a Sarracenis? Quomodo ergo laus impiorum brevis est? Sed utique brevis est, comparatione æternæ vituperationis, quam in futuro sæculo habent aut habebunt a Deo, atque ab universis sensatis ac justis. Præterea, brevis est, quia eis diu non prodest: imo veraciter nunquam prodest, et cito aliquibus sapientibus illorum vituperabilitas innotescit. Laudatores quoque eorum celeriter moriuntur ac pereunt. Ideo in Proverbiis Salomon scribit: Memoria justi cum laudibus; nomen autem impiorum putrescet.
paras.en: [[20:5|the praise of the wicked is short|Laus impiorum brevis est]]. Are not the very worst men often praised by many to the end of their life? as is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 9:24|For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul: and the unjust man is blessed|Quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ, et iniquus benedicitur]] And likewise in Proverbs: [[Prov 28:4|They that forsake the law, praise the wicked man|Qui derelinquunt legem, laudant impium]]. Further, are not Jupiter, Neptune, Venus, Diana and the other gods and goddesses of the heathen, once vicious men, praised to this day by their worshippers, the Tartars and the like, as Mahomet too is by the Saracens? How then is *the praise of the wicked short*? But it is surely short in comparison with the eternal blame which they have or will have in the world to come from God and from all who are sensible and just. Moreover, it is short because it does not profit them long: nay, in truth it never profits them, and their blameworthiness soon becomes known to some wise men. Their praisers too soon die and perish. Therefore Solomon writes in Proverbs: [[Prov 10:7|The memory of the just is with praises: and the name of the wicked shall rot|Memoria justi cum laudibus; nomen autem impiorum putrescet]]

paras.t: Et gaudium hypocritæ ad instar puncti. Omnis delectatio reproborum, carnalium et superborum in sæculo isto, velut imperceptibile punctum celerrimumque momentum est, respectu infernalium æternalium acerbissimorum suppliciorum, quæ miserrimi possidebunt. Ideo dici solet: Momentaneum quod delectat in mundo, æternum quod cruciat in inferno. Non ergo acquiescamus in vita hac stulte ac viliter delectari, ne æternaliter, inconsolabiliter, amarissime cito post hæc affligamur.
paras.en: [[20:5|and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment|Et gaudium hypocritæ ad instar puncti]] [literally *like a point*]. All the delight of the reprobate, the carnal and the proud in this world is like an imperceptible point and a most fleeting moment, compared with the eternal and most bitter torments of hell which those most wretched men will possess. Therefore it is commonly said: What delights in the world is for a moment; what torments in hell is eternal. Let us not, then, consent to take foolish and vile delight in this life, lest soon after we be afflicted eternally, inconsolably and most bitterly.

paras.t: Panis ejus in utero illius, vertetur in fel aspidum. Panis hypocritæ, est laus humana, qua pascitur, favor emolumentumque hominum, quod sortitur. Sed hic panis, in utero, id est mente ipsius, vertitur ei in fel aspidum, quia fit ei causa amaritudinis infernalis. Divitias quas devoravit, evomet. Divitiæ spirituales sunt Scripturæ divinæ: quas hypocritæ sibi nonnunquam incorporant, non plane, ut recte et humiliter vivant, sed ut docti appareant, laudem et commodum proprium sortiantur. Has ergo divitias evomunt, id est vitiose effundunt, jactant, ostentant. Et de ventre illius extrahet eas Deus, id est, de memoria ejus requiret, cur secundum ea quæ scivit et dixit, non vixit. Melius enim est, non cognoscere viam justitiæ, quam post cognitionem retrorsum reverti, ut dicit Petrus. Et Jacobus ait: Scienti bonum, et non facienti, peccatum est illi.
paras.en: [[20:14|His bread in his belly shall be turned into the gall of asps|Panis ejus in utero illius, vertetur in fel aspidum]]. The bread of the hypocrite is the praise of men, on which he feeds, and the favour and profit from men which he obtains. But this bread [[20:14|in his belly|in utero]], that is, in his mind, is turned for him into the gall of asps, for it becomes for him a cause of the bitterness of hell. [[20:15|The riches which he hath swallowed, he shall vomit up|Divitias quas devoravit, evomet]]. Spiritual riches are the divine Scriptures: which hypocrites sometimes take into themselves, not, indeed, so as to live rightly and humbly, but so as to appear learned, and to obtain praise and their own advantage. These riches, then, they vomit up, that is, they pour them out viciously, boast of them, show them off. [[20:15|and God shall draw them out of his belly|Et de ventre illius extrahet eas Deus]], that is, he will demand of his memory why he did not live according to what he knew and said. For [[2 Pet 2:21|it had been better for them not to have known the way of justice than, after they have known it, to turn back|Melius enim est, non cognoscere viam justitiæ, quam post cognitionem retrorsum reverti]], as Peter says. And James says: [[Jas 4:17|To him therefore who knoweth to do good and doth it not, to him it is sin|Scienti bonum, et non facienti, peccatum est illi]]

paras.t: Caput aspidum surget, et occidet eum lingua viperæ. Circa hoc scribit Gregorius: Aspis est parvus serpens; vipera autem est longior. Aspides quoque generant ova, ex quibus eorum filii procreantur. Viperæ vero quum conceperint, filii earum in ventrem matrum desæviunt, et ruptis matrum lateribus, generantur. Hinc vipera dicitur, quia vi parit: cujus proles cum matris exstinctione producitur. Per aspides ergo, latentes dæmonum suggestiones signantur; per linguam viperæ, violenta tentatio significatur diaboli. Caput itaque aspidum contra hypocritam surgit, quoniam primo latenti ac parva suggestione inficitur. Deinde lingua viperæ eum occidit, quia paulo post forti et impetuosa tentatione prosternitur.
